item.title: AI Search Visibility: Getting Your Local Business Cited by ChatGPT and Gemini
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
AI search visibility is how often assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Bing Copilot and Google AI Overviews name or cite your business when people ask for local recommendations. They draw on the same sources as local search: your website, Google Business Profile, reviews and directory listings. Clear, consistent facts across all of them are what earn the mention.

A growing share of local research now happens inside an AI assistant. The user asks for a good electrician nearby and gets a short list with reasoning, not ten blue links. Being absent from that list is a new kind of invisibility, and it is not fixed by the same tactics as classic rankings.

AI answers compress the results page

A traditional results page shows ten options and lets the user choose. An assistant usually names two or three and explains why. The long tail of positions four to ten effectively disappears. Google’s own AI Overviews increasingly sit above or beside the Map Pack for service questions, so the same squeeze happens inside Google.

That raises the stakes on being clearly, unambiguously described as what you are, where you are, and who you serve.

Entities matter more than keywords

Assistants reason over entities: a business, its location, its services, the areas it covers, its relationships to other things. They are not counting keyword density. If your site never states plainly what you do and where, there is nothing solid to reason about.

Structured data helps here, because it states those facts in a machine-readable form rather than leaving them to be inferred from marketing copy. LocalBusiness schema (or the right subtype, such as Dentist or Electrician) with areaServed, openingHoursSpecification and sameAs links to your profiles is the baseline. I set this up as part of technical SEO.

Get cited, not just crawled

Assistants tend to cite sources that answer a question directly and completely. Pages that bury the answer under three paragraphs of preamble get skipped in favour of ones that lead with it.

Write the answer first, then the supporting detail. It suits human readers too.

  • State the answer in the first sentence of a section
  • Use headings that match real questions
  • Keep facts consistent across your site, profile and listings

This does not replace Local SEO

Assistants draw heavily on the same underlying signals: your profile, your reviews, your citations, your site. A business invisible in Maps is usually invisible to the assistant too.

GEO is a layer on top of solid fundamentals, not a substitute. My generative engine optimization service assumes the Local SEO groundwork is in place, or fixes it first.

Where do AI assistants get local information?

They are not inventing recommendations. They draw on indexed web content, mapping data, review platforms and licensed sources. A business with a thin site, few reviews and inconsistent listings simply provides less material to draw on.

This is why GEO is not a separate discipline bolted onto SEO. The inputs overlap almost entirely; the presentation layer is what changed. A complete Google Business Profile is still one of the strongest inputs, so start with my GBP optimization checklist if yours is half-finished.

Answer one question completely

Assistants favour sources that resolve a question without needing three more pages. A page covering one topic thoroughly outperforms five pages each covering a fragment of it.

This runs against the old habit of splitting content into thin keyword-targeted pages. That tactic was already declining in classic search; in AI answers it fails outright.

  • One page per genuine question, not per keyword variation
  • Lead each section with the answer, then the detail
  • Include the specifics assistants need: areas served, hours, prices where fixed, what you actually do

In Bangladesh, remember that people ask in English, Bangla and romanised Bangla. A page that names areas the way locals do (Bashundhara R/A, Old Dhaka) gives assistants a clearer match.

Consistency across every surface

If your site says you serve five districts, your profile says three, and a directory says something else, an assistant has no reliable fact to state. It will usually name a competitor whose information agrees with itself.

This is the least glamorous work in AI visibility and the most commonly skipped. The method is the same one in my NAP consistency and citations guide.

How to check whether it is working

Ask the assistants directly. Pose the questions a customer would ask about your service and area in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot, then note whether you appear, which competitors do, and what the answer says about you.

Do it monthly and record the results. Reliable rank tracking for AI answers is still immature, so a manual log is genuinely the most honest measurement available.

AI visibility rewards clarity: say plainly what you do, where you do it, and back it with consistent signals everywhere else. For how this fits the wider picture, see the Local SEO in Bangladesh guide. Book a call if you want your current AI visibility checked.

Frequently asked questions

How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT?

Give it consistent, citable facts to work with. Keep your name, address, phone, services and areas identical across your website, Google Business Profile and major directories, earn genuine reviews, and publish pages that answer customer questions directly. There is no submission form or paid placement.

Is GEO different from SEO?

Generative engine optimization (GEO) focuses on being named and cited in AI answers rather than ranked in a list of links. The inputs overlap heavily with SEO: crawlable pages, clear entities, reviews and trusted mentions. GEO mostly changes how you structure and present information.

Do Google AI Overviews show local businesses?

Yes. For many local and service questions, AI Overviews summarise options and often sit alongside the Map Pack, which draws on Google Business Profile data. A strong profile and a website that answers questions clearly give you the best chance of appearing in both.

Does schema markup help with AI search?

It helps by stating your business facts in a machine-readable form. LocalBusiness schema with name, address, areaServed, opening hours and sameAs links removes guesswork. It will not rescue thin content or inconsistent listings, but it supports clear ones.

How can I check if AI assistants mention my business?

Ask them. Put the questions a customer would ask, such as "best AC repair service in Uttara", to ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot, and log whether you appear, who does, and what is said. Repeat monthly, because answers change.

item.title: Google Business Profile Optimization Checklist for Local Businesses
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Google Business Profile optimization means completing and maintaining every field Google reads on your listing (category, services, hours, attributes, photos, posts and reviews) so you appear for more local searches and more searchers choose you. The primary category matters most; the rest decides how relevant, active and trustworthy your profile looks next to competitors.

A Google Business Profile (formerly Google My Business) is not a directory listing you fill in once. It is the strongest ranking asset a local business owns, and Google reads roughly forty separate fields on it. Most profiles I audit are missing half of them. This is the checklist I work through, in order. If you want to understand why these fields matter for rankings first, read how Local SEO helps businesses rank on Google Maps.

Check verification, ownership and duplicates first

Before touching any field, confirm three things: the profile is verified, you (not a former agency or employee) hold the owner role, and there is only one listing for this location. Unverified profiles do not rank, and duplicates split reviews and signals between them.

  • Verification complete, including live video verification if Google asked for it
  • Owner access held by the business, with managers added as needed
  • Search your name, old name and phone number in Google Maps for duplicates

If your listing is not appearing at all, work through why a business does not show on Google Maps before optimizing anything.

Start with the primary category

Your primary category is the most important field on the whole profile. It tells Google which searches you are even eligible to appear in. Get it wrong and no amount of reviews or citations will rescue the listing.

Pick the category that describes what you are, not what you sell. A firm listed as “Contractor” when it is really an “HVAC contractor” is competing in the wrong pool entirely, and a practice set to “Medical clinic” instead of “Dentist” misses dental searches. Then add additional categories for genuine extra services, and stop. Padding the list with loosely related categories dilutes relevance rather than widening it.

Get name, address and phone exactly right

Your business name must match your real-world name. No added city, no added service. Keyword-stuffed names are one of the most common reasons profiles get suspended.

Use a local phone number that is answered during your listed hours, and an address written in the same format as on your website footer and your main directory listings. In Bangladesh, where addresses often lean on landmarks, pick one written version (road, house, area, city) and use it everywhere. My guide to NAP consistency and citations covers how to standardise it.

Fill in services and products properly

The services section is a free, structured place to tell Google exactly what you do. Each service accepts a name and a description, and those descriptions are indexed text.

Write them the way a customer would search. “Emergency drain unblocking” beats “Drainage solutions”. If your service list mirrors the language on your website’s service pages, the two reinforce each other.

  • One entry per service you genuinely offer
  • Descriptions written in customer language, not industry jargon
  • Pricing left blank unless it is fixed and accurate
  • Products added for things you sell or package (for example, “AC servicing package”)

Set service areas and booking links

Service-area businesses (plumbers, cleaners, movers, towing) should hide the street address and list the areas they actually serve, up to 20. Name real cities or neighbourhoods, such as Gulshan, Banani and Uttara, rather than drawing a vague region.

If you take bookings online, add the booking or appointment link so customers can act straight from the listing. Bookings then show up in your Performance data.

Photos and posts are activity signals

Google measures engagement, and profiles that are actively maintained outperform dormant ones with identical fundamentals. Real photos of your premises, team, vehicles and finished work carry more weight with customers than stock imagery, and they get viewed and clicked.

Add new photos every few weeks. Cover the exterior (so people recognise the place on arrival), the interior, the team at work and the results.

Reviews: velocity beats total

A steady trickle of reviews signals an operating business. Forty reviews collected in one week and none since signals a campaign. Ask every customer consistently using your review link or a QR code at the counter, reply to every review, and never buy, incentivise or filter them. Google’s policies prohibit all three.

Reply to negative reviews calmly and specifically. Future customers read the reply as much as the complaint. If you want this run for you alongside Maps ranking work, that is what my Google Business Profile optimization service covers.

Hours, attributes and skipped details

Hours seem trivial until you realise Google surfaces “open now” as a filter, and that closed businesses get pushed down at the exact moment a customer is searching. Special hours for public holidays (Eid, Pohela Boishakh, Victory Day) matter more than owners expect, because a wrong closure on a busy day costs a full day of calls.

Attributes are the checkbox list most people ignore: wheelchair access, on-site parking, appointment required, languages spoken. Each is a structured fact Google can match against a qualified search, and each is free.

  • Set special hours before every public holiday, not after
  • Fill every attribute that genuinely applies, leave the rest blank
  • If you are a service-area business, hide the address rather than faking one

The description is not a ranking field

This surprises people. The 750-character description does not directly influence ranking. Stuffing it with keywords achieves nothing except making it read badly to the humans who do see it.

Write it for conversion instead. State what you do, the areas you cover, and what makes working with you different. That is the job it actually performs.

Google Posts: small effort, real engagement

Few businesses keep posting after the first month, which is exactly why consistent posts work: they are an activity signal most competitors will not match. Use update posts for news, offer posts for promotions with dates, and event posts for anything time-bound.

You do not need marketing copy. A finished job, a seasonal reminder, a common question answered. Anything showing the business is operating.

Watch for suggested edits

Anyone can suggest an edit to your profile, and Google sometimes applies it without asking. Hours changed, category swapped, website removed. Check the profile monthly and revert anything you did not change.

How to tell whether it worked

The Performance section of your profile reports calls, direction requests, website clicks, bookings and the searches that surfaced you. Those are the numbers to watch, not your position when you search your own name.

Track them monthly. A profile that is improving usually shows rising direction requests before rising rankings, because proximity-driven discovery moves first. One client’s profile work turned into 461 calls from the Business Profile in April to August 2024, up 205% on the year before.

  • Calls and direction requests: the closest proxy for revenue
  • Discovery versus direct searches: discovery growth means new customers finding you
  • Photo views against competitors: a rough prominence gauge

Work down this list once and most profiles gain ground within weeks, because the gaps are usually basic. Keep working it monthly and the profile compounds. The profile is one part of the wider Local SEO system; the Local SEO in Bangladesh guide shows how the rest fits together. Or book a strategy call to have your profile audited.

Frequently asked questions

What is the most important part of a Google Business Profile?

The primary category. It decides which searches your listing is eligible to appear for, so a wrong one limits everything else. After that, accurate NAP, a complete services list, steady genuine reviews and correct hours have the biggest effect on whether customers find and choose you.

How often should I update my Google Business Profile?

Check it monthly at minimum, and post or add photos every week or two. Monthly checks catch suggested edits you did not make, wrong hours and new review questions. Regular posts and photos show Google and customers that the business is active.

Does the business description help my Google Maps ranking?

Not directly. The 750-character description is not treated as a ranking field, so stuffing it with keywords achieves nothing. Write it for customers: what you do, which areas you cover and why people choose you. Its job is to convert the people who read it.

Should a service-area business show its address on Google?

No, if customers do not visit you. Google's guidelines ask service-area businesses to hide the address and list the areas they serve instead, up to 20. Showing a street address you do not serve customers from is a common suspension trigger.

Can I add keywords to my business name on Google?

No. Your Google Business Profile name must match your real-world business name as it appears on signage, documents and your website. Adding cities or services to the name breaks Google's guidelines and can get the profile suspended, even if it seems to help briefly.

How do I know if my Google Business Profile optimization is working?

Watch the Performance section: calls, direction requests, website clicks, bookings and the search terms that surfaced you. Rising direction requests and discovery searches usually appear before ranking gains. A geo-grid scan then shows where in your service area visibility improved.

item.title: How Long Does Local SEO Take to Work in Bangladesh?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Local SEO in Bangladesh usually shows early movement on Google Maps within four to eight weeks of fixing the Google Business Profile, and settled results in three to six months. Quiet categories and district towns can be faster. Crowded Dhaka categories, suspended profiles and duplicate listings take longer.

It is the question every business owner asks, and the honest answer is: it depends. But ‘it depends’ is only useful if you know on what. This guide, the final part of the Local SEO in Bangladesh series, sets out a realistic timeline month by month, along with the factors that speed results up or slow them down, and the early signs that show the work is on track.

Why nobody can promise a date

Google states there is no way to pay for or request a better local ranking, and your competitors keep working while you do. So the timeline is an estimate built from your starting point, not a delivery date. How much it costs to get there is covered in part 7, How Much Does Local SEO Cost in Bangladesh?

Anyone promising first place on Google Maps within days is either describing a category with no competition or selling something that will not last.

Month one: foundations

The first month is diagnosis and repair. The profile is audited and corrected: category, services, hours, pin, photos and description. Duplicate listings are identified, and the address is standardised across the profile, website and Facebook page. If verification is incomplete, that is resolved first, because an unverified profile cannot perform. A baseline geo-grid scan and a note of current calls and direction requests in GBP Performance are taken now, so later progress can be measured honestly.

Some businesses see movement within this month, especially when the primary category was wrong or the pin was misplaced. Correcting a fundamental error can produce a jump quickly. Others see little change yet, which is normal.

Months two and three: signals build

With the foundations fixed, the work shifts to the signals that take longer: a steady review routine, citation clean-up, website service pages that match the profile, and regular photos and posts. Google needs time to recrawl, re-evaluate and trust the changes.

This is typically when geo-grid scans start to show improvement spreading outward from your location (the service-area Map Pack case study shows that pattern across 5x as many areas), and when profile actions such as calls and direction requests begin to rise.

Months four to six: results settle

By this stage, competitive categories usually show whether the strategy is working. Rankings become more stable, visibility extends further across the service area, and gains in calls and direction requests become consistent rather than occasional. For a sense of what consistent looks like, the GBP calls growth case study shows 461 calls from the profile between April and August 2024, up 205% on the same months a year earlier.

This is also when decisions are made about expanding: more service pages, more areas, or local link building to push into the tougher parts of the city.

After six months: compounding

Local SEO keeps building after the first six months if the work continues. Reviews accumulate, the website gains authority, and the business becomes more prominent locally. The effort shifts from fixing to maintaining and expanding.

Stopping entirely is possible, but competitors do not stop, and a profile left alone slowly loses ground.

What makes Local SEO faster

  • An existing, verified profile with some reviews already
  • A clear error to fix, such as a wrong category or misplaced pin
  • Low competition in your category and area
  • A website that already works well on mobile
  • An owner who responds to reviews and keeps details current

What makes it slower

  • A brand-new business with no reviews or history
  • Verification problems or a suspended profile
  • Duplicate listings that need merging or removing
  • Crowded categories in central Dhaka or Chattogram
  • No website, or a website with technical problems
  • An address written differently across many platforms

Delays specific to Bangladesh

A few issues come up here more often than elsewhere. Verification can take several attempts, particularly with video verification when the recording does not clearly show signage and proof of management. Informal or inconsistent addresses mean more clean-up. Listings created years ago by staff, or added from Maps data, may need to be claimed or merged before real work can begin.

None of these are unusual, but they add weeks, so they are worth identifying in the first audit rather than discovering later. If your profile is missing from Maps altogether, start with why your business is not showing on Google Maps.

Signs it is working

  • Profile views and search appearances rising in the performance report
  • More calls, direction requests and website clicks from the profile
  • Geo-grid scans showing visibility spreading across more of your area
  • More searches for your business name, a sign of growing awareness
  • Reviews arriving steadily rather than in rare bursts

Warning signs to watch for

  • Guaranteed rankings, or first place within days
  • Reports that show only rankings, never calls or direction requests
  • Changes to your business name that add keywords or area names
  • Reviews appearing in bulk from accounts with no history
  • No access to your own profile or reporting

Local SEO in Bangladesh usually shows early signs within weeks and delivers settled results in three to six months, with gains that keep compounding while the work continues. The timeline depends on competition, your starting point, and how consistently the fundamentals are maintained. That completes this series. Go back to any topic from the series guide above, see what the Local SEO service includes, or book a strategy call.

Frequently asked questions

How long does it take to rank on Google Maps in Bangladesh?

Early movement usually appears within four to eight weeks of fixing the profile. Stable results in competitive categories typically take three to six months. Small towns and low-competition categories can be faster, while suspended or duplicate profiles take longer.

Why is my new Google Business Profile not showing up?

New profiles often need time after verification before they appear widely, and they start with no reviews or history. Check that verification is complete, the category is right and the pin is accurate, then build reviews steadily. [Why your business is not showing on Google Maps](/blog/why-my-business-not-showing-google-maps) covers other causes.

Can Local SEO results disappear?

They can fade if the profile is neglected, details go out of date, or competitors keep improving while you stop. A suspension for breaking Google's guidelines can remove a listing entirely, which is why risky shortcuts are not worth it.

Is it faster to rank in a smaller city than in Dhaka?

Usually, yes. In most smaller cities and district towns, such as Bogura, Jashore or Rangpur, fewer competing businesses have optimised profiles, so the same work produces results sooner. Crowded categories in Gulshan, Dhanmondi or central Chattogram take longer because every nearby competitor is also investing.

Will running Google Ads make Local SEO work faster?

No. Ads and organic map pack rankings are separate systems, and Google states there is no way to pay for a better local ranking. Ads can bring calls while Local SEO builds, which is why many businesses run both for the first few months. [Local SEO vs Google Ads](/blog/local-seo-vs-google-ads-bangladesh) compares them.

item.title: How to Choose an SEO Specialist in Bangladesh
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
To choose an SEO specialist in Bangladesh, check four things before price: verifiable results (Search Console or Google Business Profile data with dates), a clear answer about what they will measure, a contract without long lock-ins where you own every account, and someone who explains the work plainly. For a local business, Local SEO experience beats agency size.

Hiring an SEO specialist in Bangladesh is difficult for one reason: the work is invisible until it is finished, and by then you have already paid. Anyone can produce a report. Far fewer can produce customers. These are the checks that separate the two, in the order they are worth doing. If you are not yet sure what the job involves, read what an SEO specialist actually does first.

Ask what they will measure first

A specialist should be able to tell you, in the first conversation, which numbers they expect to move and roughly when. Calls, direction requests, form submissions, booked jobs. If the answer is only rankings, be careful. A number one position that produces no calls is a screenshot, not a result.

Ask specifically: what does month three look like, and what does month six look like? A practitioner who has done this before will answer that comfortably, with caveats about your competition. A reseller will change the subject to packages.

Specialist or generalist?

Bangladesh has plenty of agencies offering SEO alongside paid ads, social media, design and app development. That breadth is fine for some businesses, but it means SEO is one of six things competing for the same team’s attention.

A specialist does one thing repeatedly and sees the same patterns across accounts. For a local service business, that pattern recognition matters more than agency size. I compare the two honestly in SEO specialist vs SEO agency in Bangladesh.

  • Ask what percentage of their work is SEO versus other services
  • Ask which industries they work in most often
  • Ask what they have stopped offering, and why

Look for proof you can verify

Case studies with round numbers and no source are decoration. Ask for screenshots from Google Search Console or Google Business Profile Performance, with the date range visible. Those are harder to massage than a designed report. Public reviews on platforms like Fiverr or Google, from clients you could in principle contact, add a second layer.

You can see what that should look like on my case studies page. For example, the GBP calls case study shows the Business Profile screenshot behind 461 calls from April to August 2024.

What are the red flags when hiring an SEO specialist?

  • Guaranteed first position or “page one in 30 days”
  • Bulk packages of hundreds of backlinks or directory submissions
  • Offers to write or buy reviews for you
  • Keyword-stuffed business names or fake addresses on your Google Business Profile
  • Refusing to give you admin access to your own accounts
  • Reports full of rankings for keywords nobody searches

Any one of these is enough to walk away. They produce a short-term chart and a long-term problem, sometimes a suspended profile.

Understand the contract first

Long lock-in contracts exist to protect the provider, not you. A specialist confident in the work earns the next month by delivering this one.

Ask what happens if you want to stop after ninety days. Ask who owns the Google Business Profile, the website, the Google Analytics 4 property and the Search Console account when the relationship ends. The answer should be: you do, always.

Test how they explain things

You are hiring someone whose work you cannot directly inspect, so the ability to explain it plainly is not a soft skill here; it is the main safeguard you have.

If a first conversation leaves you more confused than when you started, that will not improve once money changes hands.

Realistic price and timeline

Local SEO is not instant. Three to six months to measurable movement is normal, with compounding gains after that, and the starting condition of your profile and website changes everything. I break that down in how long Local SEO takes in Bangladesh.

On price, published entry figures in this market start around a few hundred dollars a month and rise with competition and the number of areas you need to cover. Anyone quoting a firm number before seeing your profile is quoting a package, not a plan. The full breakdown is in how much SEO costs in Bangladesh.

The best signal is simple: does this person tell you things you did not want to hear? Someone willing to say a keyword is unrealistic, or that your site needs work before rankings will move, is someone worth hiring. You can read my background, see how my Local SEO service works, or book a call and put these questions to me directly.

Frequently asked questions

How do I know if an SEO specialist is genuine?

Ask for results you can verify: Google Search Console or Google Business Profile screenshots with dates visible, or a live call where they show the data. Genuine specialists explain what they will measure, admit what they cannot promise, and let you own every account.

What questions should I ask an SEO specialist before hiring?

Ask who does the work, what they will measure in months three and six, what month one includes, who owns the accounts, what happens if you stop after 90 days, and which industries they know best. Vague answers to any of these are a warning.

Is it a red flag if an SEO specialist guarantees first position?

Yes. Nobody controls Google's rankings, and Google itself says there is no way to pay for a better local ranking. Guarantees usually mean low-value keywords, short-lived tactics like bought links, or a contract written so the promise never has to be kept.

Should I hire a local SEO specialist in Bangladesh or someone abroad?

For a Bangladesh business, a specialist who understands local search behaviour helps: searches in English, Bangla and Banglish, landmark-style addresses, mobile-first users and competition in areas like Gulshan or Uttara. Many Bangladeshi specialists also serve clients abroad, so location matters less than proof.

How long before an SEO specialist shows results?

For Local SEO, 3 to 6 months to measurable movement is normal, with gains compounding after that. Quick wins, such as fixing a wrong Google Business Profile category, can show sooner. Anyone promising page one in weeks is skipping the hard parts.

item.title: Local Citations and NAP Consistency: A Practical Guide
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
A local citation is any online mention of your business name, address and phone number (NAP), such as a Bing Places, Apple Maps, Facebook or directory listing. NAP consistency means those details match your Google Business Profile exactly everywhere. Consistent citations help Google trust your location and details, which supports Map Pack rankings; volume alone does very little.

Citations are one of the most oversold services in local SEO. Bulk packages promise hundreds of listings, most on sites nobody visits. The underlying signal is real, but the way it is usually sold is not. Here is the honest version.

What a citation actually is

A citation is any mention of your business name, address and phone number on another website. It does not need to link to you. Google uses these mentions to corroborate that your business exists, where it operates, and how to reach it. Structured citations sit in directory fields (Bing Places, Yelp, industry directories); unstructured ones appear inside articles, news sites or blog posts.

The value is corroboration, not volume. Ten consistent listings on sites Google trusts beat three hundred on directories it ignores.

Why consistency beats count

If one directory lists “Suite 4” and another lists “Unit 4”, and a third has an old phone number, Google has to decide which is correct. That uncertainty reduces confidence in your listing, and confidence feeds prominence, one of Google’s three local ranking factors alongside relevance and distance. The bigger picture is in how Local SEO helps businesses rank on Google Maps.

Pick one exact format, down to punctuation, and use it everywhere. Then match it to your Google Business Profile exactly. In Bangladesh this needs extra care, because addresses are often written several ways (road number or name, house number, landmark, area). Choose one, for example “House 12, Road 5, Dhanmondi, Dhaka 1205”, and stop improvising.

How to audit without buying tools

Search your business name in quotes, then your phone number in quotes, then any old address or number. Work through the results and record every variation you find in a simple spreadsheet. It is tedious and it works.

Fix the largest and most-trusted sources first: the major directories, your industry bodies, and anything already ranking on page one for your brand name.

  • Correct the big directories before chasing obscure ones
  • Claim listings where possible rather than submitting duplicates
  • Remove or merge genuine duplicates of your own listing, including duplicate Google profiles

Duplicate Google listings are a common reason a business drops out of Maps; I cover that in why your business is not showing on Google Maps.

When citations stop helping

Once your core listings are consistent, additional citations produce sharply diminishing returns. At that point your effort is better spent on reviews, content and links.

Anyone selling you a monthly citation package after that point is selling activity, not results.

Which directories are worth the effort?

The list is shorter than most agencies imply. Your Google Business Profile, Apple Business Connect, Bing Places for Business, Facebook, and the two or three directories that genuinely rank for your industry in your country. That covers the overwhelming majority of the value.

Beyond that you are into sites with no traffic, no editorial standards, and often no real users. Google knows which is which.

  • Data aggregators (in markets that have them) and the major mapping platforms first
  • Industry bodies and trade associations you actually belong to
  • Local chambers of commerce or city directories with real editorial oversight

Citations also feed AI answers

AI assistants such as ChatGPT search, Gemini and Perplexity build their picture of a business from the same web sources. If your directory listings disagree, they have no reliable fact to state. More on that in AI search visibility for local businesses.

Structured data reinforces citations

Citations describe you elsewhere. LocalBusiness schema states the same facts in machine-readable form on the site you control, with sameAs links pointing to your main profiles. When the two agree, confidence rises.

The name, address and phone in your schema must match your profile exactly. A mismatch there undermines the consistency you spent effort building. Schema setup is part of my technical SEO service.

Moving premises without losing rankings

A move is the most disruptive event for local rankings, because every citation you built now points at the wrong place. Handled badly it costs months.

Update the Google Business Profile first, then the site, then the major directories, then the long tail. Reverse that order and you create a window where the web disagrees with Google about where you are.

Clean up what exists, standardise the format, then move on. Citations are a foundation, not a growth lever. Your NAP should match the profile you set up using the Google Business Profile checklist, and the growth comes from the wider Local SEO system. If you want your listings audited, book a strategy call.

Frequently asked questions

What does NAP stand for in local SEO?

NAP stands for name, address and phone number. NAP consistency means those three details appear in exactly the same form on your Google Business Profile, your website and every directory that lists you. Some people add a W for website (NAPW).

How many citations does a local business need?

There is no target number. A clean, consistent set on the platforms that matter (Google, Apple Business Connect, Bing Places, Facebook and the main directories for your industry and country) covers most of the value. After that, extra listings bring sharply diminishing returns.

Do citations still help Google Maps rankings?

Yes, but less than they used to. Consistent citations help Google trust that your business exists where you say it does, which supports prominence. Reviews, your profile, website content and links now move rankings more. Inconsistent citations can still hold you back.

Should I buy a bulk citation package?

Usually not. Bulk packages submit you to hundreds of low-traffic directories Google largely ignores, and they can create duplicates you later have to clean up. Fixing and claiming the listings that already exist is cheaper and does more.

What should I do with old addresses and phone numbers online?

Update them, starting with your Google Business Profile and website, then the major directories, then smaller sites. Where you cannot edit a listing, contact the site or request removal. Search your old phone number in quotes to find listings you have forgotten.

item.title: Local SEO in Bangladesh: The Complete Guide for Local Businesses
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Local SEO in Bangladesh is the work of getting your business into the Google Maps 3-pack and local search results when nearby customers search, in English, Bangla or Banglish, for what you sell. It rests on four things: an accurate Google Business Profile, one consistent address, genuine reviews, and a website that confirms what the profile says.

More and more customers here find local businesses the same way: they pick up a phone, search Google or open Google Maps, and call one of the first few names they see. Local SEO is the work of making sure your business is one of those names. This guide covers the whole picture for a business operating here: how Google decides who appears, the problems specific to Bangladeshi addresses and search habits, what to fix first, and what it realistically costs and takes. It is part 1 of an eight-part series, and each section links to the deeper guide when you want the detail.

What Local SEO means in Bangladesh

Local SEO is the process of improving how visible your business is in searches with local intent: ‘dentist in Dhanmondi’, ‘AC repair near me’, ‘best restaurant in Sylhet’, ‘car service Chattogram’. Those searches show a map with three businesses underneath, usually called the local pack, map pack or 3-pack, followed by ordinary website results and, more and more often, an AI Overview. Local SEO covers both, but the map pack is where most of the calls come from.

It is different from general SEO because the competition is bounded by geography. A clinic in Uttara is not competing with every clinic in the country, only with the ones Google considers relevant and close to the person searching. That makes it one of the most achievable forms of search marketing for a small business, provided the basics are done properly. Part 2, What Is Local SEO?, covers the definition and the parts in more detail.

How people in Bangladesh search

Search habits here have a few features that shape the work. Nearly all local searching happens on phones, often on mobile data, so a slow website or a profile without a working call button loses people quickly. Queries are typed in English, in Bangla and in romanised Bangla, and the same person may switch between them. Area names carry a lot of weight: people search ‘Gulshan’, ‘Mirpur 10’, ‘Bashundhara R/A’ or ‘Agrabad’ far more naturally than a postcode. If most of your customers are in the capital, the Local SEO Dhaka page shows how this plays out area by area.

Google Maps itself is familiar to most smartphone users through ride-hailing and delivery apps, so people are used to looking at a map, checking reviews, and tapping to call or get directions. The business that makes those actions easy tends to win the customer.

  • Mobile first: the profile and the website are judged on a phone screen, usually on mobile data
  • Mixed language: English, Bangla and romanised Bangla queries for the same service
  • Neighbourhood names instead of postcodes: ‘dentist Dhanmondi’, ‘hotel near Zindabazar’
  • Action driven: calls and direction requests matter more than website visits

The three things Google ranks you on

Google states that local results are based mainly on relevance, distance and prominence. It also states there is no way to pay for or request a better local ranking. Every tactic in Local SEO feeds one of these three.

  • Relevance: how well your profile and website match what was searched. Categories, services, descriptions, website content and review text all contribute.
  • Distance: how far your business is from the searcher, or from the area named in the search. You cannot change where you are, but you can make sure Google has your location right.
  • Prominence: how well known and trusted Google thinks you are, judged from reviews, links, mentions across the web, and how people interact with your listing.

The step-by-step mechanics and the ranking system are covered in part 3, How Local SEO Works: Rank Higher on Google Maps.

Start with your Google Business Profile

Your Google Business Profile (formerly Google My Business) is the listing that actually appears in the map pack, so it is the first thing to get right. It is free, and a fully completed profile already puts you ahead of competitors who set up a listing years ago and never returned to it.

Verification is often the first hurdle here. Google chooses the method, and for many businesses in Bangladesh that now means recording a short video showing the signage, the premises and proof that you manage the business. Postal verification, where offered, can be slow. If a profile is suspended, fix the cause and request reinstatement through Google rather than starting again. Plan for it rather than being surprised by it, and do not create a second listing if the first one stalls, because duplicates cause more problems than they solve.

  • Business name exactly as it appears on your signage, with no added keywords or locations
  • The most specific primary category available, plus secondary categories that genuinely apply
  • Opening hours that reflect reality, including Friday hours and special hours for Ramadan and Eid
  • Every service you offer listed, with a plain description, plus attributes and a booking link if you take appointments
  • Real photos of the premises, team and work, added regularly
  • A phone number that is answered during the hours you list

The Google Business Profile optimization checklist goes through every field, and the GBP optimization service page explains how it is handled for clients.

Addresses: the Bangladesh-specific problem

Inconsistent addresses are one of the most common reasons Bangladeshi businesses underperform on Maps. The same shop might be listed as ‘House 12, Road 5, Dhanmondi’, ‘H-12, R-5, Dhanmondi R/A’ and ‘Opposite the Road 5 market’ on three different sites, in two languages. People can usually work out that these are the same place. Search engines are less forgiving, and mismatched details weaken the trust Google places in your listing.

City and area spellings add another layer. Chittagong became Chattogram, Comilla became Cumilla and Barisal became Barishal in official use, yet customers still search with both spellings. Area names vary too: Mirpur 10, Mirpur-10 and Mirpur Section 10 all appear in the wild.

  • Choose one address format and use it everywhere: profile, website, Facebook page and directories
  • Place the map pin on the actual entrance, not the centre of the building or the road
  • If there is no formal address, use the Plus Code Google Maps generates for your location
  • Mention the landmark in your description and website, not inside the address field
  • Service-area businesses that visit customers can hide their address and list up to 20 service areas instead

The local citations and NAP consistency guide explains how to find and clean up the versions of your details that already exist.

Reviews: the most underused signal

Satisfied customers in Bangladesh rarely leave a Google review on their own. They will tell friends, message you on Facebook and come back, but the review only happens if you ask. That makes a simple, consistent request process one of the most valuable things you can set up.

  • Send your Google review link by SMS or WhatsApp right after the job or visit, or print it as a QR code at the counter
  • Ask every customer, not only the ones you expect to be happy; selective asking breaks Google’s rules
  • Reviews written in Bangla are just as valuable as reviews in English
  • Reply to every review, briefly and specifically, including the negative ones
  • Never buy reviews or offer discounts in exchange for them; Google removes them and can suspend the profile

Recency matters as much as the total. A steady few reviews every month tells Google and customers more than forty that arrived in one week two years ago.

Your website still matters

For many businesses in Bangladesh, the Facebook page is the main online presence, and it may bring in most of the enquiries today. It does little for Google Maps, though. Google uses your website to confirm what your profile claims: that you offer these services, in this area, at this address. A profile linked to a thin or missing website has less to support it.

The site does not need to be large. It needs a clear page for each main service, the same name, address and phone number as your profile, contact details that work on a phone, and fast loading on mobile data, which is what Google’s Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP and CLS) measure. Structured data, using schema.org LocalBusiness or a specific subtype such as Dentist or MedicalClinic, helps search engines read your name, address, hours and service area without guessing. If you suspect the site has deeper problems, the technical SEO service page lists the usual culprits.

Citations: fewer, cleaner listings

Citations are listings of your business on other websites. In Bangladesh the list that matters is short: your Facebook page, Bing Places for Business, Apple Business Connect (which feeds Apple Maps on iPhones), relevant industry or association directories (for example BASIS for software firms or e-CAB for e-commerce businesses), your local chamber of commerce if you are a member, and any directories specific to your trade. Accuracy matters much more than volume. A handful of consistent listings beats a hundred automated submissions to sites nobody visits.

Mentions in local news sites, event listings and partner websites also count toward prominence, and they tend to come from doing something worth mentioning rather than from outreach alone.

AI search is already reading your profile

Google’s AI Overviews and assistants like ChatGPT and Gemini increasingly answer local questions directly. They draw on the same sources Local SEO improves: your Business Profile, your reviews, your website and consistent mentions elsewhere. A business with clear, consistent facts is easier for these systems to recommend. The AI search visibility guide and the generative engine optimization service cover this in depth.

Cost and timelines

Cost depends on competition, the number of locations or areas you need to rank in, the state of your current profile and website, and whether you want advice or full implementation. Packages here start from $299. The full breakdown is in part 7, How Much Does Local SEO Cost in Bangladesh?

Time follows the same factors. Profile fixes can show early movement within weeks, while competitive categories in Dhaka usually need three to six months of consistent work before results settle. Part 8, How Long Does Local SEO Take to Work in Bangladesh?, sets out what to expect month by month. For a real before and after, the GBP calls growth case study shows 461 calls from Apr–Aug 2024, up 205% on the year before.

If you are weighing Local SEO against other channels, part 6, Local SEO vs Google Ads, and part 5, Local SEO vs Traditional SEO, compare them directly.

Common mistakes

  • Adding keywords or area names to the business name on the profile
  • Two or three duplicate listings for the same location, often created by staff or customers
  • A map pin placed on the wrong building or the wrong side of a main road
  • Phone numbers that change or go unanswered, which frustrates customers and weakens trust
  • Relying entirely on Facebook, with no website for Google to verify against
  • Paying for bulk citation or backlink packages that produce nothing measurable
  • Judging progress by one keyword checked from the office, instead of across the whole service area
  • Leaving Friday, Ramadan and Eid hours unchanged, so the profile shows ‘Open now’ when the shutter is down

A simple order of work

If you are starting from scratch or from a neglected profile, this order avoids wasted effort. Each step makes the next one count for more.

  • Week one: claim or verify the profile, then fix the name, category, hours, pin and phone number
  • Weeks two to four: complete every profile field, add photos, and align the website and Facebook details
  • Month two: clean up citations and duplicates, and start a steady review request routine
  • Month three onward: build service and area content, earn local mentions, and track visibility across your area with a geo-grid

Why this matters for your business specifically is covered in part 4, Why Local SEO Is Important for Businesses in Bangladesh.

Local SEO in Bangladesh rewards the businesses that get the fundamentals right and keep them right: one accurate profile, one consistent address, a steady flow of genuine reviews, and a website that confirms what the profile says. None of it is complicated, but it does need doing properly and in the right order. If you would rather have it handled, see the Local SEO service or book a strategy call.

Frequently asked questions

Does Local SEO work in Bangladesh?

Yes. Google Maps and local search work the same way here as elsewhere, and customers use them for everything from clinics and restaurants to repair services. What differs is the detail: address formats, verification, mixed-language searches, and competition that varies a lot between Dhaka and smaller cities.

Can I rank on Google Maps without a physical shop?

Yes, if you serve customers at their location. Set up the profile as a service-area business, hide the address and list the areas you cover. You still need a real address for verification, but it is not shown publicly.

Should my Google Business Profile be in Bangla or English?

Use the business name exactly as it appears on your signage. For the description and services, write in the language your customers search in; for most commercial categories that is English, with Bangla terms where customers genuinely use them. Avoid stuffing both versions of every keyword.

How do I know if Local SEO is working?

Watch the actions in your Business Profile performance report: calls, direction requests and website clicks. Rankings checked from one spot are misleading; a geo-grid scan shows visibility across your whole service area. The Google Business Profile itself is free, so the real measure is whether those actions grow month on month.

How much does Local SEO cost in Bangladesh?

Packages start from $299 for a single-location Google Business Profile. The final figure depends on how competitive your category and area are, how many locations or service areas you need, the state of your current profile and website, and whether you want advice or full implementation.

How long does Local SEO take to work in Bangladesh?

Profile fixes can show early movement within a few weeks. Competitive categories in Dhaka usually need three to six months of consistent work before rankings and calls settle. Quieter categories and smaller cities often move faster because fewer competitors have properly optimised profiles.

item.title: How Much Does SEO and Local SEO Cost in Bangladesh?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Local SEO in Bangladesh starts from $299 for a single-location Google Business Profile package, with larger scopes quoted after an audit. The price depends on four things: how competitive your category and area are, how many locations or service areas you cover, the state of your profile and website, and how much you want done for you.

Pricing in the market runs from cheap one-off profile setups to monthly retainers for multi-branch businesses. The range is wide because the work varies so much. This guide explains what you are actually paying for, what pushes the price up or down, and how to judge whether a quote is fair. It is part 7 of the Local SEO in Bangladesh series. It covers Local SEO pricing first, then how full website SEO and Google Ads compare.

The honest answer first

There is no single price for Local SEO, and anyone quoting a firm figure before looking at your profile, website and competitors is quoting a package, not a plan. What can be said honestly is what the work involves and what makes it bigger or smaller.

For reference, Local SEO packages here start from $299, and the final figure depends on the factors below. If you are still deciding between paying for SEO and paying for clicks, read part 6, Local SEO vs Google Ads, first.

What you are paying for

Local SEO is a set of jobs. A proper engagement includes most of these, and understanding them makes quotes much easier to compare:

  • Audit: reviewing your Business Profile, website, citations, reviews and competitors, with a baseline geo-grid scan
  • Profile optimisation: categories, services, description, attributes, hours, photos and posts
  • Location clean-up: pin placement, duplicate listings and a consistent address format
  • Citations: correcting and building consistent listings on the directories that matter
  • Website work: service pages, location signals, LocalBusiness schema and mobile speed
  • Reviews: a system for asking consistently, and replying
  • Tracking and reporting: calls, direction requests and website clicks from GBP Performance, plus geo-grid visibility, explained plainly

The four things that change the price

  • Competition: a dentist in Gulshan or Dhanmondi faces far more competition than one in a district town
  • Coverage: one location and a small area costs less than several branches or a city-wide service area
  • Starting condition: a suspended profile, duplicates or a broken website mean more work up front
  • Scope: advice and a plan you implement yourself costs less than done-for-you implementation

One-off setup versus ongoing work

Some businesses need a one-time fix: a profile that was never properly set up, a wrong category, duplicate listings, an inconsistent address. That work has a clear end. Others are in competitive categories where rankings depend on a steady flow of reviews, content and local mentions, which needs ongoing effort.

A sensible approach is to start with an audit and the foundation fixes, then decide whether ongoing work is justified by the competition you face. Not every business needs a monthly retainer.

DIY: the real cost is time

Much of the foundational work can be done by an owner willing to learn: completing the profile, fixing details, uploading photos and asking for reviews. The Google Business Profile optimization checklist is a good starting point.

The cost is your time and the risk of mistakes, such as editing the business name in a way that triggers a suspension, or creating a duplicate while trying to fix verification. Where DIY usually stalls is diagnosis: working out why a well-completed profile still does not rank, and what to do about the competitors above you.

Freelancer, specialist or agency

In Bangladesh you can hire general freelancers, specialists who focus on Local SEO, or full-service agencies. Price is not the only difference. A specialist sees the same local ranking problems repeatedly; an agency may offer more services, spread across more clients and a larger team. The trade-offs are covered in SEO Specialist vs Agency in Bangladesh.

Why cheap packages cost more

At the bottom of the market, packages promise hundreds of citations, a set number of backlinks and guaranteed rankings for a price that cannot cover real work. What they usually deliver is automated directory submissions, generic content and a report of rankings for terms nobody searches. Worse, some tactics, such as keyword-stuffed business names, fake reviews or listings at virtual addresses, put the profile at risk of suspension.

A cheap package that produces nothing is expensive. A package that gets your profile suspended is very expensive.

Judge value one customer at a time

The most useful way to think about Local SEO cost is against the value of a single new customer. Work out what one new patient, client or booking is worth to you over a year. Then ask how many extra customers a month would cover the fee. For many businesses the answer is only a handful, which is what makes Local SEO good value when it is done properly.

For an example of the kind of change that is possible, the GBP calls growth case study shows calls from a Business Profile before and after optimisation. Results vary with category and area, so treat it as an illustration rather than a forecast.

Local SEO or full website SEO?

Local SEO pricing covers what wins the Map Pack: your Google Business Profile, reviews, citations and the service and location pages behind them. Full website SEO, for an online shop or a business that sells nationwide, adds keyword research at scale, content production, technical work across many pages and link earning, so it usually costs more per month. If your customers come from a city or service area, Local SEO is the part to pay for first.

SEO cost compared with Google Ads

Google Ads charges per click and stops the day the budget stops. SEO costs more effort up front, but Map Pack and organic visibility keeps producing calls without a per-click charge. Many businesses use ads to fill the gap while SEO builds. I compare the two properly in Local SEO vs Google Ads.

Questions to ask before you pay

  • What exactly happens in the first month?
  • Which numbers will you report, and how can I see them myself?
  • Who will own the Google Business Profile and any accounts you create?
  • What happens if I stop after three months?
  • Do you guarantee rankings? The right answer is no. Google states there is no way to pay for or request a better local ranking.

What the starting package covers

For transparency: the entry Google Business Profile package starts from $299 for a single location and covers the profile itself: a full audit, categories, services and products, description, attributes and hours, and photos and posts.

Keyword and geo mapping, citation clean-up, review strategy, geo-grid tracking, monthly reporting and multiple locations are scoped separately, after the profile and competition have been looked at. Details are on the GBP optimization page, and the wider scope is on the Local SEO service page.

Local SEO in Bangladesh costs what the work in front of you requires, and that depends on competition, coverage, your starting point and how much you want done for you. Judge any quote by the specific work it describes and the value of the customers it could bring, never by price alone. The final part of this series covers how long Local SEO takes to work. For a specific figure, book a strategy call.

Frequently asked questions

How much does Local SEO cost in Bangladesh?

It depends on competition, the number of locations or areas, the current state of your profile and website, and whether you want advice or full implementation. Packages here start from $299, with larger scopes quoted after an audit.

Is Local SEO a monthly cost?

Not always. Some businesses need only a one-time setup and clean-up. Businesses in competitive categories usually benefit from ongoing work, because rankings depend on a continuing flow of reviews, content and local signals, and competitors keep improving.

Can I pay for Local SEO once and stop?

You can stop at any time, and the foundation work keeps its value. What fades without ongoing effort is momentum: reviews slow down, details go out of date and competitors catch up and close the gap you built.

Why do some Local SEO packages cost so little?

Very cheap packages usually rely on automation: bulk directory submissions, template content and reports of rankings for untargeted terms. Some use tactics that risk suspending your profile. Price should reflect real work on your specific business.

What is included in a Local SEO package?

A proper package covers an audit with a baseline geo-grid scan, Google Business Profile optimisation, location and duplicate clean-up, citation work, website fixes such as service pages and LocalBusiness schema, a review routine, and reporting on calls and direction requests. Check that each item is named in the quote.

Does the Local SEO fee include Google Ads spend?

No. Local SEO fees pay for work on your profile, website and listings. Google Ads spend is a separate cost paid to Google per click, and Google states there is no way to pay for a better local ranking, so ad spend never buys a map pack position.

Is SEO cheaper than Google Ads?

Over time, usually yes per lead, because Map Pack and organic visibility keeps working without paying per click. Google Ads delivers traffic immediately but stops when the budget stops. Many businesses run ads short term while SEO builds.

Do SEO contracts in Bangladesh require a long lock-in?

Some do, but be wary of them. Long lock-ins protect the provider, not you. I work without lock-in contracts, so each month has to earn the next one. Whoever you choose, make sure you own the accounts if you leave.

item.title: Local SEO for Home Service Businesses: What Actually Drives Calls
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Local SEO for home service businesses means getting plumbers, electricians, HVAC, roofing, cleaning and pest control companies into the Google Maps 3-pack and local results across their whole service area, for urgent and planned searches alike. The essentials are the right primary category, honest service-area pages, steady reviews and call tracking tied to booked jobs.

Home service searches carry the highest intent in local search. Nobody googles “emergency plumber near me” out of curiosity. The businesses that win are not the ones with the prettiest sites; they are the ones structured to be found across an entire service area at the moment of need. For the full picture of how I approach trades, see SEO for home service companies.

Emergency intent behaves differently

Urgent searches (“24-hour electrician”, “AC not cooling”, “blocked drain open now”) convert on the first result that answers instantly. Phone number visible, hours clear, service area obvious. A beautiful site that buries the number below the fold loses to a plainer competitor that does not.

Check your own site on a phone, at arm’s length, on mobile data, and count the seconds before the number is tappable.

Set up the profile as a service-area business

Most trades do not receive customers at their premises, so the Google Business Profile should be set up as a service-area business: address hidden, up to 20 real areas listed. Choose the primary category that matches your main revenue (for example “Plumber”, “Electrician”, “HVAC contractor” or “Roofing contractor”) and add others only for services you genuinely provide.

Then fill the services list in customer language (AC servicing, gas refill, pipe leak repair, roof leak repair) and keep hours accurate, including whether you take emergency calls. My Google Business Profile checklist covers every field.

Service-area pages, done honestly

You cannot rank across a whole region from a single homepage. You need pages that genuinely address each area you serve, with real detail about the work you do there.

The dishonest version of this is spinning fifty near-identical pages with the town name swapped. Google has recognised that pattern for years and treats it as a doorway. Build fewer pages with real substance instead.

  • One page per area you actively serve, not per postcode you could reach
  • Genuine local detail: jobs done, response times, landmarks you actually cover
  • Distinct copy, not a template with the name swapped
  • LocalBusiness schema with the right subtype (Plumber, Electrician, HVACBusiness, RoofingContractor) and areaServed

Trade-specific relevance beats generic SEO

An electrician and a roofer need different content architectures because their customers search differently. Roofing is seasonal, storm-driven and high-consideration. Electrical splits between emergencies and planned work, which is why local SEO for electricians needs separate pages for emergency repairs and for projects like panel upgrades. HVAC swings between installation, servicing and summer breakdowns.

That is why I build the trade pages separately rather than as one generic service. See how it plays out for HVAC companies, plumbing businesses and roofing contractors.

Track calls, not rankings

Position is a proxy. Booked jobs are the outcome. Use call tracking so you can tell which pages and which areas actually produce revenue, then invest where it is working. Pair it with the calls and direction requests in your GBP Performance report and a geo-grid scan of each service area.

Plenty of businesses rank well in places that never convert, and poorly in the two neighbourhoods that pay the bills. On one home service account, mapping that by area led to +38% Map Pack visibility and +27% more direction requests.

Seasonality is a content calendar

Every trade has a demand curve. AC repair and servicing spike before summer, roofing after storms and the monsoon, drainage in heavy rain, pest control in the wet season. Rankings take weeks to build, so content published when demand arrives is already too late.

Work backwards. Publish and strengthen seasonal pages six to eight weeks ahead, so they are ranking when the searches start.

  • Map your demand curve from last year’s job records, not guesswork
  • Strengthen seasonal pages before the season, not during it
  • Keep them live year round; rebuilding rank every season is wasted effort

Reviews that mention the job and place

A review saying “great service” helps less than one saying “they fixed our AC in Mirpur the same day.” The second contains the service and the location in the customer’s own words, which is exactly the association you want reinforced.

You cannot script reviews and should not try, and offering discounts for them breaks Google’s policies. But asking a specific question (what did we do, and where?) tends to produce specific answers.

Response speed multiplies conversions

Ranking first is worth little if the phone rings out. For urgent trades, the business that answers wins the job regardless of who ranked above them.

Before spending on visibility, check what happens to a call at 7pm on a Saturday. Fixing that often returns more than any ranking gain.

Get the profile, service-area structure and call tracking right and home services compounds faster than almost any other local vertical. The mechanics behind it are in how Local SEO helps businesses rank on Google Maps. If you want it done for you, see my Local SEO service for small businesses or book a call to map your service area.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best way for a home service business to get more calls from Google?

Rank in the Google Maps 3-pack for your main services across the areas you serve, then make calling effortless. That means the right primary category, a hidden address with real service areas, steady reviews, one page per core service and a phone number that is answered.

Should a plumber or electrician hide their address on Google Business Profile?

Yes, if customers do not visit your premises. Google expects service-area businesses to hide the street address and list up to 20 areas served. Showing a home address as a shopfront, or using a virtual office, risks suspension.

Do home service businesses need a separate page for each area?

Only for areas you genuinely serve and want more work from. Each page needs real local detail: jobs completed there, response times, the neighbourhoods covered. Fifty near-identical pages with the town name swapped are treated as doorway pages and can hold the whole site back.

Which schema type should a home service business use?

Use the most specific LocalBusiness subtype that fits, such as Plumber, Electrician, HVACBusiness or RoofingContractor, with name, address or areaServed, telephone, openingHoursSpecification and sameAs links to your profiles. Add Service markup on individual service pages.

How long does Local SEO take for a home service company?

Expect measurable movement in about 3 to 6 months. Quick fixes like a corrected category or a merged duplicate can help within weeks, but winning competitive terms such as "AC repair near me" across a whole city takes steady review growth and content over several months.
