item.title: How Local SEO Works and Helps Businesses Rank Higher on Google Maps
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Local SEO helps a business rank higher on Google Maps by strengthening the three things Google uses to order local results: relevance, distance and prominence. In practice that means a complete Google Business Profile, a website that confirms what the profile claims, consistent citations and a steady flow of genuine reviews.

If you run a service business, Google Maps is usually the largest source of high-intent calls and visits. Yet most owners only ever see the top three results (the Map Pack) and never understand why their competitors keep showing up there instead of them. This guide covers how Local SEO works, what Google measures, and the system I use with clients to climb the Map Pack and stay there. If you want the wider background first, start with the complete guide to Local SEO in Bangladesh.

What Local SEO actually is

Local SEO is the practice of optimizing your Google Business Profile, your website and your off-site signals so that Google treats your business as the most relevant, most trustworthy and most conveniently located option for searches in a specific area. That includes “near me” searches, “in [city]” searches like “dentist in Dhanmondi”, and implicit ones where Google simply knows the searcher wants something close.

Unlike traditional SEO, which competes on a national or global keyword, Local SEO competes inside a radius. Two businesses with identical websites can rank completely differently three blocks apart, because proximity, category match and engagement change at every point on the map.

What are Google’s three local ranking factors?

Google’s own Business Profile help documentation names three factors that decide Local Pack and Maps rankings. Every tactic in this article feeds one of them:

  • Relevance: how well your profile and website match what the searcher typed. Driven by primary category, additional categories, services, on-page content and reviews that mention the service.
  • Distance: how far your business location is from the searcher, or from the place named in the search. You cannot fake this, but you can win nearby areas with stronger relevance and prominence.
  • Prominence: how well known and trusted Google thinks you are. Built from reviews and ratings, citations, backlinks, press and brand mentions, and how people interact with your listing.

Google Business Profile: the foundation

Your Google Business Profile (formerly Google My Business) is the most important asset in Local SEO. It is the listing Google ranks; your website supports it. A weak profile cannot be rescued by a great website, but a strong profile can rank even when the website is mediocre.

The non-negotiables I check on every audit:

  • Primary category set to the most specific accurate option. “Dentist” or “Air conditioning repair service” beats a broad label like “Contractor” when it describes the business.
  • Additional categories added only where they describe real services.
  • A complete services list, each with a description written in the words customers use.
  • NAP (name, address, phone) that exactly matches the website and major citations: no abbreviations, no stuffed keywords in the name.
  • Real photos added regularly: job sites, team, storefront, vehicles, before and after.
  • Google Posts published every 7 to 14 days with a clear call to action.
  • Regular and special hours kept accurate, so you show for “open now” searches.

The full field-by-field version lives in my Google Business Profile optimization checklist.

Reviews: the prominence multiplier

Reviews are the fastest lever you have for prominence. Google looks at quantity, rating, recency and what reviews say. A steady stream of recent reviews that naturally mention the job and the area outperforms a one-time burst of generic 5-stars.

Build a simple system: a short follow-up message after every completed job with a direct review link or QR code, then reply to every review, good or bad, within 48 hours. Mention the job naturally in replies; don’t stuff keywords into them. Never offer discounts or gifts for reviews and never filter who gets asked. Google’s policies prohibit both.

Citations and NAP consistency

Citations are mentions of your business on directories, industry sites and data aggregators. They no longer move rankings the way they did a decade ago, but inconsistent NAP across them still erodes trust. The goal is not “get 200 citations”; it is “make sure the ones that exist are clean and identical.”

Prioritise the platforms that matter: Apple Business Connect (Apple Maps), Bing Places for Business, Facebook, and your top 3 to 5 industry or country directories. Fix duplicates first, then expand. My guide to local citations and NAP consistency shows how to audit them without paid tools.

Website SEO that supports the Map Pack

Your website is where Google checks the claims your profile is making. If your profile says you are a roofing contractor in Chattogram, your site needs to prove it with a real service page, a clear location signal and real content depth.

The pages that matter most for local rankings:

  • A dedicated service page for every main service, not a single “Services” page listing them all.
  • A location or service-area page for each city or neighbourhood you target, with unique content, not spun copy.
  • LocalBusiness schema (or the right subtype, such as Dentist or Plumber) on the homepage and Service schema on service pages, with sameAs pointing to your profiles.
  • An embedded Google Map and your full NAP on the contact page and footer.
  • Internal links from blog content and service pages to the relevant location page, using natural anchor text.
  • Fast, mobile-friendly pages. Most local searches happen on a phone, often on mobile data.

Engagement signals: the modern tiebreaker

Once your profile and site are sound, what people do with your listing starts to matter. Calls, website clicks, direction requests, photo views and bookings all show Google that searchers find you useful. Two listings with similar fundamentals often diverge on engagement.

Practical lever: every photo, post and service description should be written to earn the click or the call. Boring profiles get ignored, and ignored profiles slide down the pack.

Where it breaks down in Bangladesh

  • Verification stalls, and the owner creates a second listing instead of resolving the first
  • Staff or agencies create listings under their own Google accounts, and access is lost when they leave
  • The business name is padded with keywords, triggering a suspension
  • The address is written differently on every platform
  • Nobody owns the profile day to day, so reviews go unanswered and hours go stale

Ownership is worth stressing: make sure the business owner, not a staff member or agency, is the primary owner of the profile. The GBP optimization checklist covers the full setup.

How do you track Google Maps rankings properly?

Because distance is part of the calculation, there is no single ranking for your business: checking from your office shows only the best case. Average position in a tool like Ahrefs tells you little about local performance, because rankings change at every point on the map, sometimes street to street. Use a geo-grid tracker (Local Falcon, BrightLocal or GMB Crush) to map visibility across a 7x7 or 9x9 grid centred on your service area. On one home service account, that grid view is how we lifted Map Pack visibility by +38% and got 5x more areas into the Top 3.

Then watch the GBP Performance metrics that correlate with revenue: calls, direction requests, website clicks and bookings. Rankings are a leading indicator; these are the result. For one client, profile work produced 461 calls from the Business Profile between April and August 2024.

The 90-day Local SEO system

  • Days 1–15: full audit of the profile, citations, on-page SEO, schema, reviews and competitors, plus a baseline geo-grid scan.
  • Days 16–45: foundation fixes: category and services rewrite, NAP cleanup, schema deployment, service and location page rebuilds.
  • Days 46–75: prominence push: a review request routine, weekly Google Posts, regular real photos, and targeted local link building.
  • Days 76–90: measure, double down on what moved the grid, and lock in the weekly routine.

Ninety days builds the foundation; how far rankings move in that window depends on competition, which I cover in how long Local SEO takes to work.

Ranking in the Map Pack is not a trick or a one-time optimization. It is a system. Get the foundation right, run the prominence loop consistently, and measure with a geo-grid instead of vanity keywords. If you would rather have it run for you, see how my Local SEO service and Google Business Profile optimization work, or book a strategy call.

Next in the Local SEO in Bangladesh series: Why Local SEO Is Important for Businesses in Bangladesh.

Frequently asked questions

How long does it take to rank on Google Maps?

Most businesses see measurable movement in 3 to 6 months. Fixing a wrong category or a duplicate listing can show results within weeks, while competitive categories in busy areas take longer because prominence (reviews, links, mentions) builds gradually. Your starting point matters more than any fixed timeline.

Can I pay Google to rank higher on Google Maps?

No. Google states there is no way to pay for or request a better local ranking. Ads can appear above the Map Pack, but they are labelled as sponsored and do not affect organic Maps positions. Organic visibility comes from relevance, distance and prominence.

Do I need a website to rank on Google Maps?

You can appear on Maps without one, but a website makes ranking much easier. Google reads the linked site to confirm what your profile claims. Dedicated service pages, area pages and LocalBusiness schema give it far more evidence than a profile alone.

Why do my Google Maps rankings change from street to street?

Distance from the searcher is one of Google's three local ranking factors, so results are recalculated for every location. You can rank first near your office and not appear two kilometres away. A geo-grid scan shows that pattern across your whole service area.

What is the difference between the Map Pack and Google Maps?

The Map Pack (or 3-pack) is the block of three local listings shown inside normal Google search results. Google Maps is the separate app and website, where more listings appear as the user scrolls. Both draw on the same Google Business Profile data and ranking factors.

item.title: Local SEO vs Google Ads: Which Is Better for Bangladesh Businesses?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Google Ads is better when you need customers immediately, are testing demand or have a short-term offer. Local SEO is better for steady, long-term customer flow at a lower cost per customer, because map pack calls have no per-click charge. For most local businesses in Bangladesh, Local SEO is the foundation and ads go selectively on top.

When a business here wants more customers from Google, it faces a choice: pay for ads and appear tomorrow, or invest in Local SEO and appear without paying per click, but later. Both have their place. This guide, part 6 of the Local SEO in Bangladesh series, compares them on the things that actually matter to a business owner: cost, speed, trust, control, and what you are left with when you stop.

How Google Ads works locally

With Google Ads you bid to appear in the sponsored positions for chosen searches, usually above the map pack. You pay each time someone clicks. You can target by location, time of day and device, link your Business Profile as a location asset so ads show your address and distance, and switch campaigns on the same day. Results are fast and measurable, and they stop the moment the budget does.

Google also offers a pay-per-lead format called Local Services Ads in some countries, but it is not available in Bangladesh, so for local businesses here paid search means standard search ads.

How Local SEO compares

Local SEO earns a position in the map pack and the ordinary results without paying per click. You invest in your Google Business Profile, reviews, website and local reputation, either with your own time or by hiring help. Results build over weeks and months and, once established, continue without a per-click cost. The mechanics are covered in how Local SEO works and ranks you on Google Maps, and the wider SEO comparison in part 5, Local SEO vs Traditional SEO.

Cost: renting versus owning

Ads are like renting a shop on a busy street: you are visible for as long as you keep paying. Local SEO is closer to buying one: slower and more effort up front, but the asset remains yours. Every click on an ad costs money; every call from your map listing costs nothing extra.

That does not make Local SEO free. It costs time or fees. But its cost per customer generally falls over time as rankings and reviews accumulate, while the cost per customer from ads tends to stay flat or rise as more competitors bid on the same searches.

Speed

Ads win on speed without question. A campaign can be running within a day. Local SEO usually shows early movement within weeks from profile fixes, with substantial results in three to six months depending on competition. See How Long Does Local SEO Take to Work in Bangladesh? for the full timeline.

Trust and attention

Many searchers recognise sponsored results, and some deliberately scroll past them to the map and the reviews. A map listing with strong reviews carries a credibility an ad cannot buy, because customers know it was earned. That said, ads appear first, and for urgent needs some people simply call the first number they see. Google also states that there is no way to pay for a better local ranking, so ad spend never buys you a place in the map pack itself.

The map pack also shows more at a glance: star rating, number of reviews, opening hours, distance and photos. An ad shows a headline and a line of text. For a customer choosing between local providers, that difference matters. In the GBP calls growth case study, an optimised profile produced 461 calls in five months without a per-click cost.

Bangladesh-specific considerations

  • Payment: Google Ads needs a payment method Google accepts, usually a credit or debit card, and some local cards need international transactions enabled first
  • Facebook ads are more familiar to many business owners here, but they interrupt people scrolling rather than answering people searching
  • In smaller cities and towns, local competition on Maps is often light, so Local SEO can pay back quickly
  • In crowded Dhaka categories, click costs rise with competition, which makes an organic position more valuable
  • Local Services Ads is not offered here, so the paid alternative is standard pay-per-click

When Google Ads is better

  • You have just opened and need customers before organic rankings build
  • You are running a time-limited offer, seasonal service or event
  • You want to test whether a new service or area has demand before investing further
  • Your category is so competitive that the map pack will take many months to reach

When Local SEO is better

  • You want steady customer flow without a monthly ad budget that never ends
  • Customers in your category compare reviews before choosing
  • Your profile and website have obvious gaps that are cheap to fix
  • You serve a defined area and want to be the default name in it
  • You have tried ads and found the cost per customer too high

Using both together

The two work well in combination. Ads can cover the searches and areas where your organic visibility is still weak while Local SEO builds. Ads data shows which searches actually convert, which guides the Local SEO work. And as the map listing strengthens, you can reduce ad spend in the areas where you already rank, rather than paying for clicks you would have received anyway. If you would rather have the organic side handled while you run the ads, see the Local SEO service.

Mistakes to avoid

  • Running ads to a profile with poor reviews, which wastes the click
  • Sending ad traffic to a slow website, or a Facebook page with no clear way to call
  • Stopping Local SEO work once ads start producing, then facing a cliff when the budget ends
  • Judging Local SEO after one month against ads that were bought to deliver instantly

Google Ads buys attention by the click; Local SEO builds a position you keep. For most businesses in Bangladesh, the sensible plan is to build the Local SEO foundation, then use ads tactically for speed, testing and gaps. Next in the series: How Much Does Local SEO Cost in Bangladesh? To see which mix suits your business, book a strategy call.

Frequently asked questions

Is Local SEO cheaper than Google Ads?

Over time, usually yes. Local SEO has an up-front cost in time or fees but no per-click charge, so the cost per customer tends to fall as results build. Ads charge for every click, indefinitely.

Can I run Google Ads from Bangladesh?

Yes. You need a Google Ads account and a payment method Google accepts, usually a credit or debit card. Some local cards need international transactions enabled before they work, so check with your bank before launching a campaign around a deadline.

Do Google Ads improve my Google Maps ranking?

No. Paid ads and organic local rankings are separate systems. Ads can bring more people to your business, but paying for ads does not raise your map pack position. Google states plainly that there is no way to pay for a better local ranking.

Should a new business start with ads or Local SEO?

Often both. Use ads for immediate customers while the Google Business Profile is set up, verified and starts collecting reviews, then shift budget toward Local SEO as organic visibility builds and the map pack starts producing calls on its own.

Can I stop Google Ads once my Local SEO is working?

Often you can reduce them. Once your Business Profile holds a Top 3 map pack position in an area, paying for clicks on the same searches there adds less. Many businesses keep a smaller budget for areas, services or seasons where organic visibility is still weak.

item.title: Local SEO vs Traditional SEO: What's the Difference?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Local SEO ranks a business, mainly through its Google Business Profile, in the map pack and on Google Maps for searches tied to a place, such as ‘dentist in Uttara’ or ‘AC repair near me’. Traditional SEO ranks web pages in the ordinary results for searches with no location attached. Most local businesses in Bangladesh need Local SEO first.

Business owners often hear ‘SEO’ and ‘Local SEO’ used as if they were the same service. They overlap, but they rank different things, in different places, for different kinds of search. Choosing the wrong one wastes months. This guide, part 5 of the Local SEO in Bangladesh series, sets out the differences plainly and helps you decide which your business needs first.

The core difference

Traditional SEO, sometimes called organic or national SEO, is about ranking web pages in the ordinary list of search results for searches with no particular location attached: ‘how to choose a laptop’, ‘best accounting software’, ‘IELTS preparation tips’. Local SEO is about ranking a business, mainly through its Google Business Profile, for searches where the location matters: ‘laptop repair Elephant Road’, ‘accountant in Motijheel’, ‘IELTS coaching near me’.

Put simply, traditional SEO competes to be the best page on a subject. Local SEO competes to be the best business in a place.

Where the results appear

  • Local SEO: the map pack of three businesses, the full local finder list, and Google Maps itself
  • Traditional SEO: the ordinary blue-link results, and increasingly the sources cited in AI Overviews
  • Both: ordinary results for local searches, where your website competes against other local sites and directories

For a search like ‘dentist in Uttara’, the map pack usually appears above the ordinary results, which is why local businesses get most of their calls from Local SEO rather than from their website’s organic position.

What each one ranks

Traditional SEO ranks pages. Each page competes on its own merits for the searches it targets, and a strong site can have hundreds of pages ranking for different topics.

Local SEO ranks listings. Your Google Business Profile is one entity, tied to one location, competing for every local search in your category. The website supports it but is not what appears in the map pack.

Ranking signals compared

SignalLocal SEOTraditional SEO
LocationCentral (distance from the searcher)Largely irrelevant
Google Business ProfileThe main assetNot a factor
ReviewsA major signalMinor
Citations and NAP consistencyImportantBarely relevant
Content depthImportantThe main factor
BacklinksImportant, with local relevance counting for moreImportant
Technical healthImportant; a broken site hurtsImportant; a broken site hurts
Structured dataLocalBusiness schema and subtypes such as DentistArticle, Product and FAQPage schema
Main measurementCalls and direction requests in GBP PerformanceClicks and impressions in Google Search Console

Keywords: with and without a place

Local keywords carry a place, either stated (‘in Chattogram’, ‘Dhanmondi’) or implied (‘near me’, or simply ‘pharmacy’ typed on a phone, which Google often treats as local). Traditional keywords do not. Volumes differ enormously as a result. A local keyword might be searched a few dozen times a month, but almost every one of those searches is a potential customer nearby. A national keyword may be searched thousands of times by people who will never buy from you.

This is also why keyword research tools often undersell local opportunity. The low numbers they show for area-specific searches hide very high purchase intent.

How success is measured

  • Local SEO: calls, direction requests, website clicks from the profile, and visibility across a geo-grid of your area
  • Traditional SEO: organic traffic, rankings for target pages, and conversions from that traffic

Mixing these up leads to bad decisions. A local business judged only on website traffic may look like it is failing while the profile quietly produces most of its calls.

Timelines and cost

Local SEO tends to show movement sooner, because the competition is limited to an area and profile fixes take effect relatively quickly. Traditional SEO is usually slower, because you compete nationally or globally and content needs time to earn links and trust. The data-driven organic growth case study shows a realistic pace: a near-invisible site taken from almost zero to 3.93K clicks and 47.4K impressions over six months.

Cost follows scope in both cases. The local side is covered in detail in How Much Does Local SEO Cost in Bangladesh? and How Long Does Local SEO Take to Work in Bangladesh?

Which one does your business need?

  • Clinics, restaurants, salons, repair services, showrooms and coaching centres: Local SEO first
  • Home service businesses that visit customers: Local SEO first, set up as a service-area business
  • E-commerce shops delivering nationwide across Dhaka, Chattogram and beyond: traditional SEO first
  • Software, IT and export businesses selling abroad: traditional SEO first
  • Businesses with branches in several cities: Local SEO for each branch, plus traditional SEO for the brand
  • Professional firms such as lawyers and accountants: both, with Local SEO usually paying back sooner

Why most need both

Part 4, Why Local SEO Is Important, covers the business case for the local side. The two disciplines support each other. Google has said that a business’s position in ordinary web results contributes to its local prominence, so a stronger website helps the profile. And content written for traditional SEO, answering customers’ questions, brings in people earlier in their decision who later search locally.

The right order for most local businesses is Local SEO first, because it produces calls soonest, followed by website content and technical work that strengthen both. The Local SEO service covers the local side, and the technical SEO service covers the website foundations: crawling, indexing and Core Web Vitals.

A quick decision checklist

  • Do customers come to you, or you to them, within a particular area? Local SEO.
  • Do you sell to anyone in the country or the world, with no local element? Traditional SEO.
  • Do people search for your service with a place name or ‘near me’? Local SEO.
  • Do people research your topic before buying, without a place in mind? Traditional SEO content.
  • Answered yes to both groups? You need both, local first.

Local SEO and traditional SEO are related disciplines aimed at different targets: one ranks a business in a place, the other ranks pages on a subject. For most businesses serving customers in Bangladesh, Local SEO comes first because it reaches the people ready to buy nearby. Next in the series: Local SEO vs Google Ads. To find out which your business needs, book a strategy call.

Frequently asked questions

Is Local SEO part of SEO?

Yes. Local SEO is a branch of SEO focused on searches with local intent. It shares techniques such as content, links and technical health, and adds its own, such as Google Business Profile optimisation, reviews and citation consistency.

Can my business rank locally and nationally at the same time?

Yes. Your Business Profile competes in local results while your website's pages compete in ordinary results. Strong pages help the profile, and a strong profile brings brand searches that help the site. Most local businesses end up running both side by side.

Which is cheaper, Local SEO or traditional SEO?

Local SEO is usually cheaper for a single-location business, because the competition is limited to an area. Traditional SEO for competitive national terms generally needs more content and link building over a longer period, so the monthly effort and total cost are usually higher.

Do I need a website for traditional SEO?

Yes. Traditional SEO ranks web pages, so there is nothing to rank without one. Local SEO can work partly without a website, though a site makes it considerably stronger because it confirms your services and location.

Are 'near me' searches part of Local SEO or traditional SEO?

They are Local SEO. A search like 'dentist near me' or 'laptop repair near me' tells Google to use the searcher's location, so it shows the map pack and ranks Business Profiles by relevance, distance and prominence. Traditional SEO only affects the website results below the map.

item.title: SEO Specialist vs SEO Agency in Bangladesh: Which Fits Your Business?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
An independent SEO specialist usually suits a local service business that needs Google Maps and search to make the phone ring: you work directly with the person doing the work, and they focus on one discipline. An agency suits businesses needing several marketing channels at once, many locations, or guaranteed cover when one person is away.

This comparison is usually written by one side to attack the other. I run as an independent specialist, so read this knowing that, and note where I say an agency is the better choice, because sometimes it plainly is.

Specialist vs agency at a glance

Independent specialistSEO agency
Who does the workThe person you hiredOften a team member assigned after the sale
FocusOne discipline, such as Local SEOSeveral services under one roof
CommunicationDirectUsually through an account manager
Cover for leave or illnessLimitedBuilt in
Best fitLocal service businesses, one or a few areasMulti-channel or multi-location operations

Where an agency genuinely wins

If you need SEO, Google Ads, social media, design and content produced simultaneously, an agency coordinates that under one roof. Managing five freelancers yourself is a job.

Agencies also survive holidays and illness. One person cannot. If your business would be damaged by two weeks of no activity, that is a real risk to weigh.

  • Multiple channels needed at once
  • Large or multi-location operations
  • Internal teams needing formal reporting structures
  • Continuity matters more than specialisation

Where a specialist wins

You talk to the person doing the work. Nothing is translated through an account manager into a brief for a junior executor, and nothing is lost in that translation.

The other advantage is focus. Someone who only does Local SEO (Google Business Profile, Map Pack rankings, service-area pages, reviews, citations) sees the same failure patterns repeatedly across accounts. That pattern recognition is difficult to buy from a generalist team spread across six disciplines. If you want to see what that daily work involves, read what an SEO specialist actually does.

The junior-executor problem

This is the specific risk with agencies, and it is worth naming plainly. The person who sells you the work is frequently not the person who does it. You are impressed in the meeting, then the account is handed to whoever has capacity.

It is not always the case, and good agencies avoid it. But it is worth asking directly: who will actually be working on my account, and how many other accounts do they hold?

Is a specialist cheaper than an agency?

Specialists are often assumed to be cheaper. Sometimes true, sometimes not. An experienced independent may charge more per hour than an agency junior, and be better value because fewer hours are wasted.

Compare what is actually delivered per month rather than headline rates. Ask both what specifically happens in month one. My honest breakdown of SEO cost in Bangladesh covers what moves the price.

Questions that work on both

The same questions expose weak providers regardless of structure. Who does the work. What gets measured. What happens if I leave in ninety days. Who owns the accounts. Show me a result with the source visible, like the ones on my case studies page.

A strong answer to all five matters more than whether the answer comes from one person or twelve. The full checklist is in how to choose an SEO specialist in Bangladesh.

Choose the structure that matches the problem. Multi-channel and multi-location, an agency probably fits. Local service business that needs the phone to ring, a specialist usually goes deeper for less. If that is you, read how I work, see what my Local SEO service covers, or book a strategy call.

Frequently asked questions

Is a freelance SEO specialist cheaper than an agency in Bangladesh?

Often, but not always. An independent specialist has lower overheads, yet an experienced one may charge more per hour than an agency junior. Compare what is delivered each month, and who delivers it, rather than the headline rate.

When should a business choose an SEO agency over a specialist?

Choose an agency when you need several channels at once (SEO, Google Ads, social media, design), run many locations, need formal reporting for an internal team, or cannot risk a pause when one person is ill or on leave.

When is an independent SEO specialist the better choice?

When you are a local service business that needs calls from Google Maps and search, want to speak directly to the person doing the work, and value deep experience in one discipline over a broad team. Most single-location and small multi-area businesses fit this.

What should I ask both a specialist and an agency?

Who will actually work on my account and how many others they handle, what gets measured, what happens in month one, what happens if I stop after 90 days, who owns the accounts, and can you show a result with the source visible.

item.title: What Does an SEO Specialist Actually Do All Day?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
An SEO specialist improves how often a business appears in Google search and Google Maps for the searches that bring customers. The work runs in a cycle: audit the website and Google Business Profile, fix technical problems, build relevant pages, strengthen reviews and citations, then measure calls and enquiries. For local businesses, the profile and Map Pack come first.

Business owners rarely get a straight answer about what SEO work consists of. Partly because it varies, and partly because vagueness protects margins. This is the honest version: what the work is, roughly in the order it happens. It is written from the Local SEO side, because that is what I do; if the term is new to you, start with what Local SEO is.

Weeks one and two: the diagnosis

Nothing gets fixed before the diagnosis. That means auditing the Google Business Profile field by field, checking the website for technical faults (crawling, indexing, mobile speed, Core Web Vitals), mapping which keywords you already rank for in Google Search Console, and running a geo-grid to see your visibility across the whole service area rather than from one address.

Keyword research happens here too: what customers actually type, including “near me”, “in [area]”, “cost” and “emergency” variations, and in Bangladesh the Bangla and Banglish versions.

Most audits surface the same handful of problems: wrong primary category, incomplete profile fields, inconsistent business details across the web, and a website with no pages targeting the services people actually search for.

The Google Business Profile work

For a local business this is the part with the most impact, and the part most often left half-finished. Categories, services with written descriptions, products, attributes, opening hours, holiday hours, photos, posts and service areas.

It is unglamorous and it moves rankings. The full field-by-field list is in the GBP optimization checklist.

  • Primary category correct, additional categories genuine
  • Every service listed with a description in customer language
  • Real photos of the business, not stock
  • Hours and special hours accurate, suggested edits checked monthly

The website work

Maps rankings are not decided by the profile alone. Google reads the linked website to judge relevance and trust, so a one-page site gives it very little to work with.

That means service pages that go into genuine depth, area pages where you truly operate, title tags and H1s that say what each page is about, internal links that connect them, LocalBusiness schema stating the business facts in machine-readable form, and fixing whatever technical faults the audit found. That last part is covered in detail on my technical SEO service page.

Off-site: citations, reviews, mentions

Your business details need to agree across the directories Google trusts. Inconsistency there reduces its confidence in your listing, and confidence feeds prominence. The audit method is in my citations and NAP consistency guide.

Reviews are the other half. Not buying them, which is both against policy and obvious, but building a repeatable habit of asking. Steady beats sudden. Local links and mentions (suppliers, associations, local news) round it out.

Ongoing: measure, adjust, repeat

After the foundations, the work becomes a loop. Check the geo-grid for weak zones, look at which searches are surfacing the profile, see which pages produce calls, and put effort where the data points. That loop is how one home service client reached +38% Map Pack visibility across its service areas.

The reporting should be readable in two minutes and tie rankings to calls, direction requests and form leads from GBP Performance and GA4. If it takes an analyst to interpret, it is not reporting; it is decoration.

What a specialist should not do

Buying links. Buying reviews. Spinning fifty near-identical location pages with the town name swapped. Stuffing keywords into the business name. Promising a number one position. Any of these will produce a short-term chart and a long-term problem.

If someone offers guaranteed rankings, they either misunderstand how Google ranks results or are counting on you not checking. Google says plainly that nobody can pay for a better local ranking. My guide to choosing an SEO specialist lists the other red flags.

None of this is secret. It is just laborious, and doing it consistently is what separates results from activity. Whether one person or a team should do it is covered in specialist vs agency. To see how I package the work, look at my Local SEO service or book a strategy call.

Frequently asked questions

What is the main job of an SEO specialist?

To get a business found by the people searching for what it sells, and turn that into enquiries. Day to day that means auditing the site and Google Business Profile, researching keywords, fixing technical problems, improving content, building trust signals and reporting on calls, leads and traffic.

What is the difference between an SEO specialist and a Local SEO specialist?

A general SEO specialist focuses on organic rankings for a website, often nationally. A Local SEO specialist also works on the Google Business Profile, Map Pack rankings, service areas, reviews and citations, because local results depend on distance and prominence as well as the website.

What tools does an SEO specialist use?

Google Search Console, Google Analytics 4 and the Google Business Profile dashboard are the core free tools. Most specialists add a crawler for technical audits, a keyword research tool and, for local work, a geo-grid rank tracker. Tools support the work; they do not replace judgement.

How many hours does SEO take each month?

It depends on competition and scope. The first one or two months are heaviest because of auditing and fixing foundations. After that the work becomes a steady loop of content, profile updates, review follow-up and measurement. Ask any provider what specific tasks month one includes.

Can I do SEO myself instead of hiring a specialist?

Yes, for the basics. Completing your Google Business Profile, asking for reviews and keeping NAP consistent need time more than expertise. Technical fixes, competitive keyword strategy and diagnosing ranking drops are where a specialist usually saves more time and money than they cost.

item.title: What Is Local SEO? A Practical Guide for Bangladesh Businesses
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Local SEO (local search engine optimization) is the work of making your business appear, and look like the right choice, when someone nearby searches Google or Google Maps for what you sell. In Bangladesh that means a verified Google Business Profile, an accurate address and map pin, genuine reviews, consistent listings and a website that backs them up.

Local SEO gets described in so much jargon that many business owners here assume it is either very technical or a kind of advertising. It is neither. This guide explains what Local SEO actually is, what it is made of, what it is not, and which businesses benefit most, with examples from the way people here really search.

Being found and being chosen

The definition above has two halves and both matter. Appearing is about ranking: being one of the businesses Google shows. Looking like the right choice is about what the searcher sees when you do appear: your reviews, photos, hours, and whether calling you is one tap away. Ranking without the second half produces views but not customers.

What a local search result looks like

Search ‘dentist near me’ or ‘AC servicing Mirpur’ on your phone and you will usually see three kinds of result. At the top there may be ads, marked as sponsored. Below them sits a map with three businesses listed underneath, known as the local pack or map pack. Below that come the ordinary website results. Tapping ‘more places’ opens the full list on Google Maps, called the local finder. On many searches an AI Overview now sits above all of it, summarising options drawn from the same profiles and reviews.

Local SEO targets the map pack and the local finder first, because that is where people call, ask for directions and compare reviews. It also targets the ordinary results below, where your website competes.

  • Ads: paid placement, gone the moment the budget stops
  • Map pack: the three businesses under the map, earned through Local SEO
  • Organic results: website listings, earned through website SEO
  • Google Maps app: the same local rankings, searched directly inside Maps

The parts that make up Local SEO

Local SEO is a collection of related jobs rather than one task. For a typical business in Bangladesh they are:

  • Google Business Profile: the listing itself (formerly Google My Business), with categories, services, attributes, hours, photos and posts
  • Location accuracy: a correct address, map pin and service area, written the same way everywhere
  • Reviews: a steady flow of genuine customer reviews, with replies
  • Website: pages that confirm your services and location, LocalBusiness schema markup, and fast loading on a phone
  • Citations: consistent listings on Facebook, Bing Places and relevant directories
  • Local prominence: mentions and links from local news, associations and partners
  • Measurement: tracking calls, direction requests and visibility across your area

The complete Local SEO in Bangladesh guide, part 1 of this series, goes through each of these in order. If you want a single field-by-field list for the profile, use the Google Business Profile optimization checklist.

What Local SEO is not

  • It is not social media marketing. A busy Facebook page helps your business, but it does not rank you on Google Maps.
  • It is not advertising. You do not pay Google per click, and results do not stop when a budget runs out.
  • It is not a one-time listing. Profiles, reviews and competitors change constantly.
  • It is not a trick. Fake reviews, keyword-stuffed business names and fake addresses get profiles suspended.
  • It is not the same as ranking a website nationally. The competition is limited to your area.

The difference from general website SEO is explained fully in Local SEO vs Traditional SEO.

Which businesses need it most

Any business that serves customers in a particular place benefits. It matters most where people search with urgency, or compare options nearby before choosing:

  • Clinics, diagnostic centres, dentists and pharmacies
  • Restaurants, cafes, bakeries and sweet shops
  • Salons, parlours, gyms and spas
  • Coaching centres, language schools and training institutes
  • Repair and home services: AC, electrical, plumbing, pest control, car repair, mobile and laptop repair
  • Showrooms: furniture, electronics, motorcycles, tiles and sanitary ware
  • Hotels, resorts and community centres
  • Law firms, accountants, travel agencies and real estate offices

Businesses without a shopfront

Many Bangladeshi businesses serve customers at home: technicians, cleaners, tutors, caterers, event decorators. Google supports this. You set the profile up as a service-area business, hide your address from the public, and list the areas you cover (up to 20).

You still compete on relevance and prominence, and your real base still influences where you rank strongest, so be realistic about how far from it you can compete. A technician based in Mohammadpur will find it easier to rank there than in Uttara, however the service area is set.

An example of how it plays out

Take a hypothetical dental clinic in Dhanmondi. Someone two roads away searches ‘dentist near me’ at nine in the evening. Google looks for dental businesses that are relevant (the right category, services and reviews mentioning treatment), close to that phone’s location, and prominent (well reviewed and widely referenced). It also considers whether the clinic is open right now.

If the clinic’s profile lists ‘Medical clinic’ instead of ‘Dentist’, shows no evening hours, and has its map pin on the wrong street, it may not appear at all, even though it is the nearest dentist. Fix those three things and it becomes a real candidate. That, in miniature, is Local SEO.

How to tell whether it is working

Your Google Business Profile has a performance report that shows how many people found your profile, what they searched, and what they did next. The numbers that matter most are the actions: calls, direction requests and website clicks. Compare them month on month.

Rankings are useful as a leading indicator, but checking one keyword from your own shop tells you very little, because results change with the searcher’s location. A geo-grid scan checks your position across a grid of points covering your service area and gives a far more honest picture. The service-area visibility case study shows what that looks like in practice: 5x more areas in the Top 3 and +38% Map Pack visibility.

Where to start this week

  • Search for your business on Google Maps and check that the name, pin, hours and phone number are right
  • Look for duplicate listings of your business and note them
  • Compare your primary category with the top three competitors in your area
  • Add ten real photos of your premises, team or work
  • Send your review link to five recent customers

If your business does not appear at all, why your business is not showing on Google Maps covers the usual causes.

Local SEO is the discipline of being findable and choosable in your own area. For a business in Bangladesh it starts with an accurate, complete Google Business Profile and grows through reviews, a supporting website and consistency across the web. Next in the series: How Local SEO Works: Rank Higher on Google Maps. Or see how the Local SEO service works.

Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between Local SEO and Google Maps SEO?

They are mostly the same thing. Google Maps SEO usually refers to ranking in the map pack and on Maps, which is the core of Local SEO. Local SEO also includes the website work that helps you rank in ordinary local results.

Is Local SEO only for big cities like Dhaka?

No. It often works faster in smaller cities and towns, where fewer businesses have optimised profiles. The same principles of relevance, distance and prominence apply in Khulna, Rajshahi, Sylhet, Barishal or a district town, and the competition there is usually lighter than in Gulshan or Dhanmondi.

Do I need a website for Local SEO?

You can appear on Google Maps without one, but a website strengthens your profile considerably. It confirms your services and location to Google, carries your LocalBusiness schema, and gives customers somewhere to check you before they call.

Can I do Local SEO myself?

The basics, yes: completing your profile, fixing your details and asking for reviews. The harder parts are diagnosing why you are not ranking, cleaning up duplicates and citations, and sustaining the work every month without letting it slide.

Is Local SEO the same as Google My Business?

No. Google My Business is the old name for Google Business Profile, the free listing that appears on Maps. Optimising that profile is the biggest single part of Local SEO, but Local SEO also covers reviews, citations, your website, schema markup and how visibility is measured across your area.

Does Local SEO work for 'near me' searches?

Yes, that is exactly what it targets. When someone types 'dentist near me' or 'AC repair near me', Google uses the phone's location and shows nearby businesses it finds relevant and trustworthy. You do not need 'near me' written anywhere; you need an accurate profile and location.

item.title: Why Local SEO Is Important for Businesses in Bangladesh
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Local SEO is important for businesses in Bangladesh because customers already search Google and Google Maps for nearby services, mostly on their phones, and call one of the first three businesses they see. A well-run Google Business Profile captures that ready-to-buy demand without paying per click, and the results keep building over time.

Every day, people in your area search Google for exactly what you sell. Some of them find you. Most of them, unless you have done something about it, find the three businesses Google shows first. This guide, part 4 of the Local SEO in Bangladesh series, explains why Local SEO has become one of the most important marketing investments for businesses here, and, just as usefully, when it is not the priority.

Customers are already searching

Local SEO does not create demand. It captures demand that already exists. Someone searching ‘AC repair Mirpur’ in May, ‘pharmacy open now’ late at night, or ‘best biryani near me’ at lunchtime, has already decided to buy. The same intent shows up in Bangla and romanised Bangla searches too. The only open question is from whom. The businesses in the map pack get the first look, the first call and usually the sale.

That makes Local SEO fundamentally different from most marketing, which interrupts people who were not looking. Here you are answering people who asked. Part 3, How Local SEO Works: Rank Higher on Google Maps, explains how Google picks the three businesses that get that first look.

Local searches carry high intent

A search with a place in it, or typed on a phone for something nearby, usually comes from someone close to a decision. They are not researching a topic for later. They want a clinic that is open, a technician who can come today, a restaurant for tonight. That is why a small number of local searches can be worth more to a business than a large volume of general website traffic.

Google Maps is the default directory

For a generation of smartphone users in Bangladesh, Google Maps is where you check where something is, whether it is open, and what other people thought of it. The printed directories and signboard-only discovery that once worked have faded. If your business is not on Maps, or looks neglected there, you are invisible at exactly the moment customers are choosing.

Facebook alone is not enough

Facebook is a strong channel in Bangladesh and many businesses rely on it. But a Facebook page mainly reaches people who already follow you, see a shared post, or are shown an ad. Someone searching Google for a service near them does not see your Facebook activity at all. Local SEO reaches the customers who have never heard of you, at the moment they are ready.

The two work well together. Customers who find you on Maps often check your Facebook page before calling, so keeping both accurate and consistent pays twice.

Results compound instead of stopping

Paid ads stop the moment you stop paying. The work that improves your Local SEO keeps working: a well-built profile, a body of genuine reviews, a website Google trusts and consistent listings across the web all accumulate. Each month builds on the last. That is why Local SEO is often described as an asset rather than an expense. The comparison is laid out in full in Local SEO vs Google Ads.

Trust is decided before the first call

Customers in Bangladesh are cautious with new providers, and reasonably so. Before they call, they check reviews, look at photos and see how the business responds to complaints. A profile with recent reviews, a solid star rating, real photos of the premises and thoughtful owner replies does much of the selling before any conversation happens. Local SEO builds exactly those signals.

Uneven competition is an opportunity

In many categories and areas, especially outside central Dhaka, it is common to find competing profiles with the wrong category, missing hours, few photos and unanswered reviews. Doing the fundamentals properly can be enough to move ahead of competitors who have been in business far longer.

In crowded categories in Dhaka the bar is higher and the work takes longer. Even there, the businesses that invest consistently tend to pull ahead of those that do not.

It also feeds AI search

Google’s AI Overviews and assistants such as ChatGPT and Gemini now answer questions like ‘which clinic in Gulshan is good for children’. They rely on the same sources Local SEO strengthens: Business Profiles, reviews, websites and consistent mentions. Investing in Local SEO now also positions you for how people will search next. See AI search visibility for local businesses.

The business case

The clearest way to judge Local SEO is against the value of a single customer. If one new patient, client or booking is worth a meaningful amount to you over time, then even a handful of extra calls a month covers the cost of the work. That is the calculation to make, rather than comparing providers’ prices in isolation.

Results vary widely with category, area and starting point. For a real example of what the change can look like, the GBP calls growth case study shows a profile’s call volume taken from the Business Profile performance report.

When it is not the priority

  • You sell only online, nationwide, with no local presence or service area
  • Nobody searches for what you offer yet, because the product or service is new to the market
  • Your business cannot answer the phone or take on more customers right now
  • Your operations have problems that reviews will expose; fix those first

In those cases other channels may do more, and it is better to say so than to sell work that will not pay back.

Local SEO matters in Bangladesh because it puts you in front of people who are already looking, builds trust before the first conversation, and keeps paying back long after the work is done. For most businesses serving a local area, it is one of the highest-return marketing investments available. Next in the series: Local SEO vs Traditional SEO. Or see what the Local SEO service includes.

Frequently asked questions

Is Local SEO worth it for a small business in Bangladesh?

For most small businesses that serve a local area, yes. The core tool, a Google Business Profile, is free, and the work compounds over time. It is worth it when the value of a few extra customers each month exceeds the cost of the work.

Is Facebook enough, or do I need Google as well?

Facebook reaches your followers and people shown your posts or ads. Google reaches people actively searching for a service near them, including those who have never heard of you. Most local businesses benefit from both.

Which businesses benefit most from Local SEO in Bangladesh?

Businesses where customers search with urgency or compare options nearby benefit most: clinics, dentists, restaurants, salons, coaching centres, AC and electrical repair services, showrooms, hotels and professional services such as lawyers and accountants. If people search for you with an area name or 'near me', Local SEO is worth doing.

Can Local SEO help if my business is in a small town?

Yes, often more than in big cities. Competition in district towns and smaller cities such as Bogura, Jashore or Rangpur is usually lighter, and many rival profiles have the wrong category or no reviews, so a properly optimised profile can stand out quickly.

Do I need Local SEO if customers already know my business?

Yes, if you want new customers. People who already know you search your name, but new customers search the service: 'diagnostic centre near me' or 'AC servicing Uttara'. Local SEO is what puts you in those category searches, where you compete with every nearby alternative.

item.title: Why Your Business Is Not Showing Up on Google Maps
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
If your business is not showing on Google Maps, the cause is usually one of a short list: the profile is unverified or suspended, the primary category is wrong, a duplicate listing is splitting signals, your details are inconsistent across the web, the website is too thin, or you are checking from the wrong place. Diagnose which applies first.

Not showing up on Google Maps feels like one problem, but it is at least nine different ones with different fixes. Diagnosing the right cause first saves months. Here is how I work through it, starting with the quickest checks.

Are you checking from the wrong place?

Map Pack results change street by street. Searching from your office and seeing yourself ranked first tells you almost nothing, because distance to the searcher is a ranking factor you cannot control. The reverse is also true: searching from home and not seeing yourself does not mean you are invisible everywhere.

Use a geo-grid tool that samples results across your whole service area instead of a single point. Almost every business that believes it ranks well is looking at one favourable pin. That grid view is also how we tracked 5x more service areas reaching the Top 3 on one home service account.

The profile is unverified or suspended

Unverified profiles do not rank. Verification can stall if Google asks for live video verification and it is never completed. Suspended profiles vanish entirely, often without an obvious notification. Check the status in your dashboard before assuming a ranking problem.

Common suspension triggers: a virtual office address, a keyword-stuffed business name, or a service-area business displaying a street address it does not operate from. Reinstatement means fixing the cause first, then submitting a request with proof such as a trade licence, signage photos and utility bills.

Your primary category is wrong

Covered in the GBP optimization checklist, but worth repeating because it is the most common silent killer. A wrong primary category means you are invisible for the searches that matter, no matter how strong everything else is. A dental practice set to “Medical clinic” will struggle to appear for “dentist near me”.

Inconsistent NAP across the web

Name, address and phone number appearing differently across directories weakens Google’s confidence that those listings describe the same business. That uncertainty costs you prominence.

Audit your citations, pick one canonical format, and fix the largest directories first. The process is laid out in my local citations and NAP consistency guide.

The website underneath is too weak

Maps ranking is not decided by the profile alone. Google reads the linked website for topical relevance and trust. A one-page site with no service or location pages gives it very little to work with. Slow mobile pages, blocked crawling or pages missing from Google’s index make it worse.

This is where Maps work and website SEO stop being separate projects. If the site has indexing or speed problems, technical SEO fixes come before content.

You are new, and prominence takes time

Prominence builds from reviews, citations, links and engagement. A profile created last month competing against one that has been active for eight years is not losing on optimization; it is losing on history. That gap closes, but not in a fortnight. For realistic expectations, see how long Local SEO takes to work.

Duplicate listings are splitting signals

Businesses that have moved, rebranded, or been listed by a previous agency often have two or three profiles competing with each other. Google splits reviews and signals between them, and sometimes ranks the wrong one.

Search your business name, your old name and your phone number in Maps directly. Claim or merge anything you find. This alone has recovered rankings for businesses that assumed they had a content problem.

Google is filtering you out

When several similar businesses share an address or building (common in Dhaka plazas and medical centres), Google often shows one and filters the rest for the same search. Zoom into the map or open the Local Finder: if you appear there but not in the 3-pack, filtering is a likely cause. Stronger relevance and prominence for your own listing is the fix, not a fake suite number.

Your service area is drawn wrong

Service-area businesses list up to 20 areas. Too wide and you spread relevance across places you will never realistically serve. Too narrow and you disappear from areas you want. Remember that the service area does not override distance: Google still measures from your verified location.

Define it honestly around where you actually take jobs. Twenty genuine neighbourhoods beats a hundred aspirational ones.

A competitor is filing edits against you

Anyone can suggest an edit to your profile, and Google sometimes applies it without asking. Hours changed, category swapped, marked permanently closed. It happens more than most owners realise, and occasionally it is deliberate.

Check your profile monthly. If something changed that you did not change, revert it and report it.

Work through these in order rather than fixing everything at once, or you will never know what moved. Once the cause is fixed, how Local SEO lifts Maps rankings explains what to build next. If you would rather have it diagnosed properly, get a free visibility audit, see my Google Business Profile optimization service, or look at how the full Local SEO system works.

Frequently asked questions

Why can I find my business by name but not by service on Google Maps?

Because a name search only proves the listing exists. Showing for a service search like "plumber near me" depends on relevance, distance and prominence. A wrong primary category, a thin website or few reviews usually explains the gap, and so does checking from only one location.

How long does it take for a new Google Business Profile to show on Maps?

A verified profile usually appears for its own name within days. Ranking for competitive service searches takes longer, often 3 to 6 months, because prominence (reviews, links, mentions) has to build up. Verification problems or duplicate listings can delay it further.

How do I know if my Google Business Profile is suspended?

Sign in to the profile and check its status. A suspended profile shows a notice and either disappears from Maps or can no longer be edited. Fix the cause (often a keyword-stuffed name or an address you do not serve customers from), then submit a reinstatement request with evidence.

Can a competitor make my business disappear from Google Maps?

They can try. Anyone can suggest edits, such as marking you closed or changing your category, and Google sometimes applies them. Fake reviews and spam reports also happen. Check your profile monthly, revert unwanted changes and report clear abuse through Google's support channels.

Why did my business suddenly drop off Google Maps?

The usual causes are a suspension, an accepted suggested edit, a new duplicate listing, a change of address or category, or Google filtering similar listings in the same building. Check the profile status and recent edits first, then search your phone number for duplicates.

item.title: Starting at 16: What Being the Youngest SEO Expert in Bangladesh Taught Me
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
I’m Ratul Roy. I started working on SEO at sixteen, which is why people call me the youngest SEO expert in Bangladesh. Today I work as an independent Local SEO expert in Bangladesh, I founded DigiPolli, and I am a Fiverr Level 2 seller with a 4.9★ rating from 243 reviews.

That age gets described as being the youngest SEO expert in Bangladesh, which is a label other people applied rather than one I chose. What matters more than the age is what starting that early actually changes about how you work.

No formal training meant no inherited assumptions

I did not learn SEO from a course that was already out of date when it was recorded. I learned by changing something on a real site and watching what happened, which is slower and produces fewer confident opinions.

That turns out to be an advantage in a field where much of the received wisdom is several algorithm updates behind. If you never learned the old rule, you do not have to unlearn it.

Balancing education with client work

I studied at Gov PC College and later ICT at Islamic University while taking freelance projects. That is a difficult combination and I would not pretend otherwise, but it forced a habit that stuck: only work on what demonstrably moves a number, because there is no spare time for anything else.

Two years working as an SEO Strategist on competitive campaigns filled in what solo freelancing could not teach, mainly how larger accounts fail and how they are structured. If you are curious what that work looks like day to day, I wrote it up in what an SEO specialist actually does.

Why I narrowed to Local SEO

The early work covered everything: e-commerce, content sites, general organic growth. Some of that produced results I am still proud of, and you can see them on the case studies page.

But local work suited me better, because the feedback loop is short and honest. A business either gets more calls or it does not. There is no arguing with a phone that rings more than it did last month. The GBP calls growth case study is the clearest example: 461 calls from one Google Business Profile between April and August 2024.

That focus is now the whole of my Local SEO service: Google Business Profile, Maps rankings, citations, reviews and the website pages that support them, for businesses in Bangladesh and abroad.

What being young cost, and what it did not

It cost credibility in first conversations. People make assumptions, reasonably, about experience and age. The only answer is showing verifiable results rather than arguing about it.

It did not cost quality of work, and I would push back on the idea that it might. Search does not know how old you are. It responds to whether the profile is complete, the site is sound, and the signals are consistent.

What I would tell a business owner

Do not hire on age in either direction. Hire on whether the person can show you a result with the source visible, explain their plan without jargon, and tell you something you did not want to hear.

Those three hold regardless of who is sitting across from you. I set out the rest of the checks in how to choose an SEO specialist in Bangladesh.

The label matters less than the record. Read more about the background, or book a call and judge from the conversation.

Frequently asked questions

Who is called the youngest SEO expert in Bangladesh?

The label is often applied to me, Ratul Roy, because I started working on SEO at sixteen. I did not choose it. Today I am an independent Local SEO expert in Bangladesh and the founder of DigiPolli.

Where is Ratul Roy based, and who does he work with?

I am a Local SEO expert in Bangladesh. I work directly with local businesses in Bangladesh and with service businesses worldwide, mostly on Google Business Profile, Google Maps rankings and the websites that support them.

Is Ratul Roy a verified Fiverr seller?

Yes. I am a Fiverr Level 2 seller with a 4.9★ rating from 243 reviews. Those reviews are public on the platform, which is one of the simplest ways to check a freelancer's record before hiring.

Does age matter when hiring an SEO specialist?

Not in either direction. Google does not know how old you are. Judge any specialist on whether they can show results with the source visible, explain their plan without jargon, and tell you something you did not want to hear.

What does Ratul Roy specialise in now?

Local SEO: Google Business Profile optimisation, Google Maps and map pack rankings, citations and NAP consistency, review systems, and the technical and on-page website work that supports them. Packages start from $299, with no lock-in contracts and white-hat methods only.
